taxonomy.title: Esophagus — motility and achalasia

review.title: Interpret a visible pressure tracing

cues.phrase: Achalasia
cues.why: Weak option-form outlier: this is the sole one-word label, against two longer anatomical diagnostic names. An odd-one-out guess can favor it, but brevity does not reliably identify correctness. These are authentic names in the same diagnostic category; padding the key would not improve the item. This is not a substantive reason to reject this foundational item.

fairness: Reviewed exact after version question.achalasia.manometric-recognition.v1.r5. This report covers all 11 entries in the supplied round-three packet; the brief's reference to 16 does not match that file. Judgments use the after Presentation, Current update, Exhibit and its referenced image, Task and Options. Titles, before fields, explanations, author self-checks and prior PASS labels were not evidence for solving an item. Runtime sequencing, wait displays and finite profiles are outside this requested review scope.
Original flag fully resolved: YES for the mapped picture request. No separate in-game question flag is attached to this item.

Owner note fully resolved: YES, b1-B01, 'There will be a picture?' The referenced local PNG exists and was visually inspected. It shows synchronous body-channel events, labels the junction observation, and is explicitly a constructed schematic. This verifies the artifact, not its rendering inside a live game.

Achalasia is the defensible best offered diagnosis when the absent traveling contraction and elevated junction relaxation measurement are combined. The alternatives require different interpretation of the body/relaxation findings. The absence of a fixed luminal lesion is relevant context rather than a disguised exclusion of one of these three motility diagnoses. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified at this qualitative classification level.

Too easy for a routine PGY-2/3 challenge: the accessible description explicitly states that no peak travels, leaving familiar manometric recognition. Combining two measurements into one diagnostic label is not two consequential reasoning steps. PASS relies on the standard's explicitly accepted B01 foundational role, not on relabelling this as moderate or hard.

All verdicts in this report are editorial predictions, not measured resident performance or clinical approval. No network or fresh guideline verification was performed. Drafts remain needs_clinician_review; exact clinical sign-off belongs to Melissa Rowland.
suggestions: Retain the accepted foundational classification and accessible raw observations; do not claim resident-level two-step difficulty for this version.

Keep the natural diagnostic names rather than adding words solely to equalize option length. Preserve this exact frozen version; a different resident application objective would need a separately reviewed version.

review.title: Investigate the junction wall before treating the motor pattern

cues.phrase: Endoscopic ultrasound with wall sampling
cues.why: Weak category/specificity cue: the key is the sole option that obtains tissue; the two competitors measure functional obstruction. A test-wise reader may favor sampling after the malignancy/thickening narrative. However, all three are concrete investigations, and the narrative never says that tissue sampling is required. Recognizing why this category takes priority over clarifying the discordant physiology is the legitimate clinical inference.

fairness: Reviewed exact after version question.achalasia.manometric-recognition.v2.r6.
Original flag fully resolved: YES for the mapped objection to nonspecific treatment-assessment options. No separate in-game question flag is attached.

Owner note fully resolved: YES, b1-B02. Every choice now names an actual investigation. Heller and PPI were examples of specificity in the owner's note, not instructions to use those treatments regardless of the findings.

The learner must reconcile an obstructive motor presentation with continued weight loss, junction-crossing resistance and eccentric cardia thickening despite benign mucosal samples, then prioritize investigation of the wall. This gives endoscopic ultrasound with sampling a defensible advantage over the two physiological studies. Benign mucosal sampling does not itself settle the deeper structural concern.

The supine/upright discrepancy keeps FLIP or timed esophagram clinically credible as physiological corroboration; they are not absurd tests. The structural findings establish why that is not the most pressing unresolved issue here. The pressure table alone cannot be treated as definitive proof of primary achalasia.

No confident clinical inaccuracy or missing discriminator among these three choices identified. The key does not claim that a malignancy is already proven. Moderate rather than hard: the structural warning findings are prominent, but a resident anchored on the pressure study has a plausible competing next step.
suggestions: Retain the concrete procedures, discordant physiology and tissue-depth distinction. Do not add a sentence naming pseudoachalasia or announcing the need for wall sampling.
Preserve this exact frozen version. Clinical approval of the investigation and sampling wording remains separate from this editorial PASS.

review.title: Dysphagia: read the reports, then choose the next target
fairness: Cover-the-key attack did not identify a reliable nonmedical shortcut. All three choices are named diagnostic procedures with a with-phrase describing their assessment, and their lengths are comparable. No choice contains a teaching rationale or an absolute. Upper endoscopy and Endoscopic ultrasound share a word root, but the completed endoscopy does not itself identify which different procedure should come next. That overlap is not sufficient to select the key.

The focal wall finding, continued weight loss and resistance at the junction support investigating a secondary structural process despite the negative mucosal result. Endoscopic ultrasound with guided sampling is the defensible best next procedure among these choices because it can assess the wall target and obtain tissue. The presentation does not prove malignancy, and the key should not be explained as if malignancy were already established.

The two functional tests are credible alternatives for further characterization of outflow/emptying in a patient with these symptoms and pressure observations. Neither directly resolves the stated wall abnormality and limited mucosal evidence. Their potential usefulness later does not make either the best next procedure in this particular record. The ranking remains an offline clinical judgment for Melissa's exact-version sign-off, not a claim of newly verified guidance.

Two consequential steps are present: interpret why a mucosal biopsy without malignant cells does not settle an asymmetric wall abnormality, then prioritize evaluation/sampling of that structural target over further functional confirmation. The pressure findings make anchoring on a primary motor disorder a credible competing error. For a typical PGY-2/3, this is moderate rather than hard; a resident who recognizes this structural-versus-functional distinction can answer quickly.

The pressure rows do not establish an exact motor subtype or cancer diagnosis, and the task does not require either. I would not infer a new pressure cutoff, a quantified malignancy risk or a mandated sampling device from this text. No confident clinical inaccuracy was identified within this limited offline review.

The owner clarity note is resolved by concrete, separately labelled observations: the scope encountered resistance, sampled mucosa contained no identified malignant cells, and CT showed one-sided wall thickening crossing the junction. The pressure acquisitions are separated by position. No pre-answer label such as achalasia or pseudoachalasia supplies the interpretation. This judges readability of the supplied text exhibit, not the existence or rendering of an imaging asset.

Necessary observations are present for this next-test decision. The current weight-loss update reinforces the concern, but the asymmetric wall finding and mucosal sampling limitation carry the main discrimination. Absence of an amount or duration of weight loss does not prevent choosing among these three procedures. Runtime wait displays and unseen prior nodes are outside the permitted after-field review.
suggestions: No mandatory wording rewrite for this exact node. Retain the concrete CT and tissue-sampling observations, the functional-testing alternatives and the neutral next-procedure task.

Keep any post-answer explanation explicit that further assessment is warranted, not that the record already proves a secondary malignancy or a particular motor subtype. Preserve needs_clinician_review until Melissa approves the exact version.

decisionNodes.stem: Which acquisition should determine {patientName}'s esophageal-body classification?

answerChoices.label: Single wet swallows after baseline recovery
answerChoices.rationale: Separated swallows assess ordinary swallow-induced peristalsis; overlapping swallows can inhibit a developing contraction.

answerChoices.label: Multiple rapid swallows followed by a recovery swallow
answerChoices.rationale: This probes inhibition and contractile reserve rather than replacing the baseline series needed to classify the body pattern.

answerChoices.label: Upright rapid drinking followed by clearance swallows
answerChoices.rationale: This is an outflow challenge and does not replace separated baseline swallows for the disputed peristaltic classification.

decisionNodes.explanation: The acquisition sequence changes how absence of contraction is interpreted. A swallow delivered during the preceding response can inhibit that response; a rapid-swallow maneuver is not an ordinary separated-swallow series. Use baseline wet swallows separated by recovery before assigning the body classification. Provocative sequences have additional roles.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At the return visit, {patientName} reports continued unintentional weight loss.
decisionNodes.stem: Which procedure should be requested next for {patientName}'s swallowing problem?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic ultrasound with guided sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The motor pattern can coexist with a secondary junction process. Weight loss, one-sided wall thickening and resistance despite unrevealing mucosal samples make wall assessment and directed tissue acquisition the next target.

answerChoices.label: Functional lumen imaging with distensibility measurement
answerChoices.rationale: The positional pressure difference could tempt further functional testing. A distensibility measurement would not determine what accounts for the focal CT wall abnormality beyond the sampled mucosa.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium swallow with tablet passage
answerChoices.rationale: Quantifying emptying is credible for a motility question. It would not establish the cause of the focal junction-wall finding that remains unresolved after the mucosal samples.

decisionNodes.explanation: The primary pressure acquisition can support an achalasia motor pattern despite the upright reference-range value. That pattern does not establish a primary cause. Interpret the focal wall finding, weight loss and resistance together with the limited mucosal sample: endoscopic ultrasound can assess and sample the wall target. Another emptying or distensibility measurement addresses function rather than that unresolved target.

case.learningSummary: The acquisition sequence changes how absence of contraction is interpreted. A swallow delivered during the preceding response can inhibit that response; a rapid-swallow maneuver is not an ordinary separated-swallow series. Use baseline wet swallows separated by recovery before assigning the body classification. Provocative sequences have additional roles. The primary pressure acquisition can support an achalasia motor pattern despite the upright reference-range value. That pattern does not establish a primary cause. Interpret the focal wall finding, weight loss and resistance together with the limited mucosal sample: endoscopic ultrasound can assess and sample the wall target. Another emptying or distensibility measurement addresses function rather than that unresolved target.

decisionNodes.stem: Which report of the pressure study should accompany {patientName}’s timed esophagram request?

answerChoices.label: Reduced post-swallow reserve with preserved junction relaxation
answerChoices.rationale: The software-integrated recovery responses do not augment the baseline despite taller peaks. Baseline propagation and the liquid-load relaxation observations do not establish absent body contractility or impaired junction relaxation.

answerChoices.label: Preserved post-swallow reserve with preserved junction relaxation
answerChoices.rationale: The junction component fits, but peak height is not the integrated contractile response. The measured recovery integrals do not demonstrate augmentation.

answerChoices.label: Absent esophageal body contractility with impaired junction relaxation
answerChoices.rationale: This mistakes the quiet clustered-swallow phase for baseline failure and the presence of dysphagia for junction obstruction. Traveling baseline waves and the recorded relaxation behavior contradict those claims.

decisionNodes.explanation: Read the separate measurements for their separate purposes. The integrated post-sequence contraction, rather than its peak alone, is the reserve comparison. The baseline waves show propagation, and the junction trace during liquid loading does not support impaired relaxation. Report reduced reserve with preserved relaxation. The common timed-esophagram request assesses actual emptying; this question does not claim that a reserve result selects barium over every other investigation or proves the cause of dysphagia.

exhibit.caption: Constructed pressure study and software integration; schematic traces, not patient measurements.
exhibit.description: The baseline upper, middle and lower body peaks occur successively. During each clustered-swallow sequence the body channels are quiet, followed by a taller, narrower recovery peak. The software DCI bars for both recovery responses are shorter than the baseline DCI bar. During the liquid load, the junction relaxation trace lies within the shaded laboratory reference band and the body channels do not form a sustained simultaneous pressure column.

decisionNodes.explanation: The failed/premature body activity with impaired junction relaxation is an achalasia-like spastic pattern. question.explanation: The failed/premature body activity with impaired junction relaxation is an achalasia-like spastic pattern. decisionNodes.stem: Which acquisition should determine {patientName}'s esophageal-body classification?

answerChoices.label: Single wet swallows after baseline recovery
answerChoices.rationale: Separated swallows assess ordinary swallow-induced peristalsis; overlapping swallows can inhibit a developing contraction.

answerChoices.label: Multiple rapid swallows followed by a recovery swallow
answerChoices.rationale: This probes inhibition and contractile reserve rather than replacing the baseline series needed to classify the body pattern.

answerChoices.label: Upright rapid drinking followed by clearance swallows
answerChoices.rationale: This is an outflow challenge and does not replace separated baseline swallows for the disputed peristaltic classification.

decisionNodes.explanation: The acquisition sequence changes how absence of contraction is interpreted. A swallow delivered during the preceding response can inhibit that response; a rapid-swallow maneuver is not an ordinary separated-swallow series. Use baseline wet swallows separated by recovery before assigning the body classification. Provocative sequences have additional roles.

exhibit.caption: Investigation record

items.label: Upper endoscopy
items.value: No mucosal mass or fixed luminal narrowing. Resistance when the scope crossed the gastroesophageal junction.

items.label: Junction mucosal biopsy
items.value: Mucosa present; malignant cells not identified.

items.label: CT: gastric cardia and junction
items.value: Wall thickening is greater on one side and extends across the gastroesophageal junction.

items.label: Pressure study: primary supine series
items.value: Catheter spans the junction. Median relaxation pressure above this laboratory's upper reference limit during separated water swallows.

items.label: Pressure study: upright series
items.value: Median relaxation pressure within this laboratory's reference interval.

items.label: Pressure study: body channels
items.value: No propagated distal contractions in either position.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic ultrasound with guided sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The motor pattern can coexist with a secondary junction process. Weight loss, one-sided wall thickening and resistance despite unrevealing mucosal samples make wall assessment and directed tissue acquisition the next target.

answerChoices.label: Functional lumen imaging with distensibility measurement
answerChoices.rationale: The positional pressure difference could tempt further functional testing. A distensibility measurement would not determine what accounts for the focal CT wall abnormality beyond the sampled mucosa.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium swallow with tablet passage
answerChoices.rationale: Quantifying emptying is credible for a motility question. It would not establish the cause of the focal junction-wall finding that remains unresolved after the mucosal samples.

decisionNodes.explanation: The primary pressure acquisition can support an achalasia motor pattern despite the upright reference-range value. That pattern does not establish a primary cause. Interpret the focal wall finding, weight loss and resistance together with the limited mucosal sample: endoscopic ultrasound can assess and sample the wall target. Another emptying or distensibility measurement addresses function rather than that unresolved target.

Endoscopic ultrasonography can assess and sample tissue beyond the mucosa. Neither another emptying study nor a distensibility study resolves the new wall finding.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The outside acquisition log records a catheter crossing the junction. The saved sequences show successive water swallows beginning before the preceding response has ended. Body pressure remains low during each sequence; a distal contraction follows its end.
decisionNodes.stem: Which acquisition should be requested to classify {patientName}’s esophageal body motility?

answerChoices.label: Separated single-water-swallow pressure series
answerChoices.rationale: The existing sequences test inhibition and recovery; they do not supply a separated baseline series for body classification.

answerChoices.label: Repeated multiple-rapid-swallow pressure series
answerChoices.rationale: More rapid sequences may reproduce inhibition and recovery but do not supply the missing baseline classification.

answerChoices.label: Continuous rapid-water-drinking pressure series
answerChoices.rationale: A liquid-load challenge addresses outflow under a different load rather than replacing baseline peristaltic assessment.

decisionNodes.explanation: Interpret what was acquired, not simply how many traces were saved. Inhibition during rapid swallowing and a recovery contraction are not a diagnostic baseline body series. Request separated single-water swallows for that classification. A rapid-drink acquisition answers a different physiological question. This task selects the required acquisition; it does not impose a universal repeat-manometry-versus-barium sequence after catheter intolerance.

resultGateAfter.resultNarrative: The esophageal pressure-study report is available for review.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At return, {patientName} reports continuing unintentional weight loss. The endoscopy record describes resistance as the instrument crossed the junction; mucosal samples contain no malignancy. An interval CT shows eccentric thickening of the gastric cardia extending across the junction.
decisionNodes.stem: Which procedure should be requested next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic ultrasound with wall sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The motor pattern does not exclude a secondary junction process. Eccentric wall thickening and resistance despite unrevealing mucosal samples make deeper wall assessment the priority among these procedures.

answerChoices.label: Functional lumen imaging probe distensibility study
answerChoices.rationale: This can complement equivocal motor assessment, but another distensibility measurement does not establish the cause of the focal wall abnormality.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium esophagram with a tablet
answerChoices.rationale: This can characterize bolus emptying, but the new wall finding requires etiologic tissue assessment rather than another measure of impaired passage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Separate recognition of the motor pattern from attribution to primary disease. The primary-position study can support an achalasia pattern despite the upright value, but the wall abnormality and weight trajectory require evaluation for a secondary junction lesion. Endoscopic ultrasonography can assess and sample tissue beyond the mucosa. Neither another emptying study nor a distensibility study resolves the new wall finding.

answerChoices.label: Reduced contraction reserve; obtain a timed barium esophagram
answerChoices.rationale: The reduced recovery integral concerns reserve, not proof of a junction obstruction. Assess actual emptying before selecting junction-disrupting treatment.

answerChoices.rationale: The reserve finding does not itself establish an outflow lesion that would justify dilation.

answerChoices.rationale: This both overcalls augmentation and converts discomfort into an unsupported indication to disrupt the junction.

No superiority over FLIP or every other corroborating test is claimed.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Medication reconciliation shows that {patientName} takes oxycodone regularly for back pain and took it before the pressure study. The prescribing team can supervise a medication adjustment, and the patient can maintain oral intake during reassessment.
decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation and next plan best fit {patientName}'s record?

answerChoices.label: Achalasia-like spastic pattern; reassess after coordinated opioid withdrawal
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes the pattern and the potentially reversible medication-associated contribution before committing to irreversible therapy.

answerChoices.label: Achalasia-like spastic pattern; proceed to myotomy planning while continuing the opioid
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes the tracing but treats it as sufficient proof of a primary irreversible disorder despite a relevant drug exposure.

answerChoices.label: Distal-spasm pattern; coordinate opioid withdrawal and reassessment before myotomy planning
answerChoices.rationale: Notices the medication issue but ignores the abnormal junction relaxation when classifying the tracing.

answerChoices.label: Distal-spasm pattern; proceed to myotomy planning while continuing the opioid
answerChoices.rationale: Combines an incorrect relaxation-pattern classification with premature invasive treatment planning during the relevant exposure.

decisionNodes.explanation: The failed/premature body activity with impaired junction relaxation is an achalasia-like spastic pattern. Opioids can produce this phenotype; Chicago v4 advises studying off opioids when possible. Coordinate a clinically appropriate withdrawal/reassessment plan before treating this as established primary disease requiring myotomy. No abrupt cessation or fixed washout is prescribed.

decisionNodes.stem: Which esophageal pressure acquisition should be repeated for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Multiple-rapid-swallow pressure acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: The clustered block records the inhibitory phase but stops before its recovery response can be assessed. A repeat that includes the post-sequence recording can answer the remaining reserve question; silence during the cluster is not a completed negative reserve result.

answerChoices.label: Upright single-water-swallow pressure acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: The worksheet already establishes a technically recorded upright baseline series. Its weak but traveling waves are observations to interpret, rather than a reason to substitute another baseline for the truncated provocative block.

answerChoices.label: Rapid-drink challenge pressure acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: The during-load interval supplies outflow observations even though this acquisition also stops at its last water event. Repeating that different physiological question does not recover the post-cluster response needed to interpret the other block.

decisionNodes.explanation: Identify the purpose and the recorded extent of each block. Both challenge acquisitions stop at their final water event. The liquid-load interval contains outflow observations, whereas the clustered-swallow acquisition does not contain the post-sequence contraction needed for reserve assessment. Repeat the multiple-rapid-swallow acquisition through recovery rather than report that reserve was absent. This does not declare every possible rapid-drink protocol question complete. The later returned full study is a new assessment, not an interpretation of this truncated acquisition.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At return, {patientName} reports continuing unintentional weight loss. The endoscopy record describes resistance as the instrument crossed the junction; mucosal samples contain no malignancy. An interval CT shows eccentric thickening of the gastric cardia extending across the junction.
decisionNodes.stem: Which procedure should be requested next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic ultrasound with wall sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The motor pattern does not exclude a secondary junction process. Eccentric wall thickening and resistance despite unrevealing mucosal samples make deeper wall assessment the priority among these procedures.

answerChoices.label: Functional lumen imaging probe distensibility study
answerChoices.rationale: This can complement equivocal motor assessment, but another distensibility measurement does not establish the cause of the focal wall abnormality.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium esophagram with a tablet
answerChoices.rationale: This can characterize bolus emptying, but the new wall finding requires etiologic tissue assessment rather than another measure of impaired passage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Separate recognition of the motor pattern from attribution to primary disease. The primary-position study can support an achalasia pattern despite the upright value, but the wall abnormality and weight trajectory require evaluation for a secondary junction lesion. Endoscopic ultrasonography can assess and sample tissue beyond the mucosa. Neither another emptying study nor a distensibility study resolves the new wall finding.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The foregut team is reviewing the earlier outside pressure study before operative planning. The acquisition worksheet records the catheter spanning the junction in each block.
decisionNodes.stem: Which esophageal pressure acquisition should be repeated for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Multiple-rapid-swallow pressure acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: The clustered block records the inhibitory phase but stops before its recovery response can be assessed. A repeat that includes the post-sequence recording can answer the remaining reserve question; silence during the cluster is not a completed negative reserve result.

answerChoices.label: Upright single-water-swallow pressure acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: The worksheet already establishes a technically recorded upright baseline series. Its weak but traveling waves are observations to interpret, rather than a reason to substitute another baseline for the truncated provocative block.

answerChoices.label: Rapid-drink challenge pressure acquisition
answerChoices.rationale: The during-load interval supplies outflow observations even though this acquisition also stops at its last water event. Repeating that different physiological question does not recover the post-cluster response needed to interpret the other block.

decisionNodes.explanation: Identify the purpose and the recorded extent of each block. Both challenge acquisitions stop at their final water event. The liquid-load interval contains outflow observations, whereas the clustered-swallow acquisition does not contain the post-sequence contraction needed for reserve assessment. Repeat the multiple-rapid-swallow acquisition through recovery rather than report that reserve was absent. This does not declare every possible rapid-drink protocol question complete. The later returned full study is a new assessment, not an interpretation of this truncated acquisition.

exhibit.caption: Outside acquisition record
cells: A
Individual water events, recorded in supine and upright positions
A weak pressure wave travels down the body after each event; the junction trace falls within the laboratory relaxation interval. Recording continues between events.
B
A cluster of water events
Body channels become quiet during the cluster. Acquisition stops at the final water-event marker.
C
A continuous water load
Junction relaxation is within the laboratory interval, without a sustained body-wide pressure column. Acquisition stops at the final water-event marker.

decisionNodes.stem: Which procedure should be requested next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic ultrasound with wall sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The motor pattern does not exclude a secondary junction process. Eccentric wall thickening and resistance despite unrevealing mucosal samples make deeper wall assessment the priority among these procedures.

answerChoices.label: Functional lumen imaging probe distensibility study
answerChoices.rationale: This can complement equivocal motor assessment, but another distensibility measurement does not establish the cause of the focal wall abnormality.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium esophagram with a tablet
answerChoices.rationale: This can characterize bolus emptying, but the new wall finding requires etiologic tissue assessment rather than another measure of impaired passage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Separate recognition of the motor pattern from attribution to primary disease. The primary-position study can support an achalasia pattern despite the upright value, but the wall abnormality and weight trajectory require evaluation for a secondary junction lesion. Endoscopic ultrasonography can assess and sample tissue beyond the mucosa. Neither another emptying study nor a distensibility study resolves the new wall finding.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The catheter tip remains above the diaphragm throughout the outside recording. Blind advancement stopped after repeated retching. During swallows, pressure rises simultaneously in the recorded esophageal channels.
decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should guide procedural planning for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Endoscopically assisted manometry
answerChoices.rationale: Junction-crossing manometry can provide the relaxation and body measurements absent from this recording. Assisted placement addresses the documented technical failure.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium esophagram with a barium tablet
answerChoices.rationale: Emptying and tablet passage can corroborate obstruction, but the prior contrast study already shows retention and this does not provide the missing manometric phenotype.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Regurgitation can tempt reflux testing, but it does not resolve junction relaxation and contractile classification after this technically failed pressure study.

decisionNodes.explanation: The observed pressure events cannot classify junction relaxation when the catheter has not crossed it. Assisted catheter placement can permit the manometric assessment needed for procedural planning. Contrast emptying and reflux monitoring answer other questions. This comparison makes no claim that manometry universally precedes FLIP after every failed attempt.

decisionNodes.stem: Which acquisition should determine {patientName}'s esophageal-body classification?

answerChoices.label: Single wet swallows after baseline recovery
answerChoices.rationale: Separated swallows assess ordinary swallow-induced peristalsis; overlapping swallows can inhibit a developing contraction.

answerChoices.label: Multiple rapid swallows followed by a recovery swallow
answerChoices.rationale: This probes inhibition and contractile reserve rather than replacing the baseline series needed to classify the body pattern.

answerChoices.label: Upright rapid drinking followed by clearance swallows
answerChoices.rationale: This is an outflow challenge and does not replace separated baseline swallows for the disputed peristaltic classification.

decisionNodes.explanation: The acquisition sequence changes how absence of contraction is interpreted. decisionNodes.currentUpdate: An earlier technically adequate pressure study includes separated swallows and two repeat rapid-swallow sequences. The draft report describes both provocative responses as normal. The recorded observations are shown below.
decisionNodes.stem: Which change should be requested in {patientName}'s draft report?

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; retain the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: Normal inhibition during the sequence is not evidence of post-sequence augmentation. The repeat responses challenge the reserve conclusion, whereas reproduced discomfort without the supplied outflow findings does not establish liquid-load obstruction.

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: This accepts suppression as proof of reserve and lets symptom reproduction override the actual junction and pressure observations during loading.

answerChoices.label: Revise the reserve conclusion; revise the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: The reserve conclusion needs correction, but the symptom-provoking liquid load does not itself supply evidence for the added outflow revision.

answerChoices.label: Retain the reserve conclusion; retain the outflow conclusion
answerChoices.rationale: Baseline propagation and appropriate inhibition do not establish the post-sequence reserve response. Accepting the whole draft misses that distinction.

decisionNodes.explanation: A provocative protocol has distinct acquisition phases. Appropriate inhibition while swallowing does not establish augmentation after the sequence; the repeated post-sequence finding warrants correction of the reserve statement. A familiar symptom during rapid drinking does not by itself establish impaired outflow. This report review does not assign a final motor diagnosis or a cause of all symptoms.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: A provocative protocol has distinct acquisition phases. decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation and next plan best fit {patientName}'s record?

answerChoices.label: Achalasia-like spastic pattern; reassess after coordinated opioid withdrawal
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes the pattern and the potentially reversible medication-associated contribution before committing to irreversible therapy.

answerChoices.label: Achalasia-like spastic pattern; proceed to myotomy planning while continuing the opioid
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes the tracing but treats it as sufficient proof of a primary irreversible disorder despite a relevant drug exposure.

answerChoices.label: Distal-spasm pattern; coordinate opioid withdrawal and reassessment before myotomy planning
answerChoices.rationale: Notices the medication issue but ignores the abnormal junction relaxation when classifying the tracing.

answerChoices.label: Distal-spasm pattern; proceed to myotomy planning while continuing the opioid
answerChoices.rationale: Combines an incorrect relaxation-pattern classification with premature invasive treatment planning during the relevant exposure.

decisionNodes.explanation: The failed/premature body activity with impaired junction relaxation is an achalasia-like spastic pattern. Opioids can produce this phenotype; Chicago v4 advises studying off opioids when possible. Coordinate a clinically appropriate withdrawal/reassessment plan before treating this as established primary disease requiring myotomy. No abrupt cessation or fixed washout is prescribed.

answerChoices.label: Achalasia-like spastic pattern; reassess after coordinated opioid withdrawal
answerChoices.rationale: Recognizes the pattern and the potentially reversible medication-associated contribution before committing to irreversible therapy.

answerChoices.rationale: Notices the medication issue but ignores the abnormal junction relaxation when classifying the tracing.

answerChoices.label: Distal-spasm pattern; proceed to myotomy planning while continuing the opioid
answerChoices.rationale: Combines an incorrect relaxation-pattern classification with premature invasive treatment planning during the relevant exposure.

decisionNodes.explanation: The failed/premature body activity with impaired junction relaxation is an achalasia-like spastic pattern. Opioids can produce this phenotype; Chicago v4 advises studying off opioids when possible. Coordinate a clinically appropriate withdrawal/reassessment plan before treating this as established primary disease requiring myotomy. No abrupt cessation or fixed washout is prescribed.

answerChoices.rationale: The rapid sequence cannot substitute for an adequate baseline series. Completing the physiologic assessment prevents treatment planning from an unclassifiable acquisition.

answerChoices.rationale: This can assess emptying and corroborate obstruction, but does not supply the missing separated-swallow body classification.

answerChoices.rationale: Reflux monitoring answers a different remaining question and does not replace the missing baseline motility acquisition.

decisionNodes.stem: Which treatment should be offered to {patientName} on the basis of this workup?

answerChoices.label: Laparoscopic Heller myotomy
answerChoices.rationale: The adequate primary-position study establishes absent peristalsis with impaired junction relaxation. Myotomy is an established junction-directed treatment.

answerChoices.label: Oral omeprazole therapy
answerChoices.rationale: Reflux-directed acid suppression does not treat the demonstrated junction-relaxation and body-motility problem. A normal upright pressure does not erase the adequate primary-series findings.

answerChoices.label: Oral isosorbide dinitrate therapy
answerChoices.rationale: Pharmacological junction relaxation is a less effective palliative approach, rather than the preferred durable treatment for a routine procedural candidate. It can have a role when definitive options are unsuitable.

decisionNodes.explanation: The primary series has abnormal junction relaxation and failed contractions throughout; the upright measurement does not impose the both-position rule for EGJOO on this pattern. Offer a junction-directed definitive treatment. Heller myotomy is the appropriate offered procedure; pneumatic dilation and POEM are also legitimate options in suitable patients but are not compared here. Omeprazole does not correct this physiology, and nitrate therapy is generally a palliative option when definitive therapy is unsuitable.

case.learningSummary: A rapid-swallow sequence can inhibit contractions and show a recovery response. It is not the baseline series needed to classify this patient’s body motility. Repeat HRM with an adequate separated-swallow protocol before acting on an apparent absent-contraction pattern; contrast emptying and reflux monitoring answer related but different questions. The primary series has abnormal junction relaxation and failed contractions throughout; the upright measurement does not impose the both-position rule for EGJOO on this pattern. Offer a junction-directed definitive treatment. Heller myotomy is the appropriate offered procedure; pneumatic dilation and POEM are also legitimate options in suitable patients but are not compared here. Omeprazole does not correct this physiology, and nitrate therapy is generally a palliative option when definitive therapy is unsuitable.

answerChoices.label: Reduced contraction reserve with preserved liquid-load outflow
answerChoices.rationale: Lack of post-sequence augmentation on both repeats indicates reduced reserve; symptoms during drinking do not by themselves establish outflow obstruction when the pressure observations remain reassuring.

answerChoices.label: Preserved contraction reserve with impaired liquid-load outflow
answerChoices.rationale: This treats inhibition during swallowing as evidence of post-swallow reserve and treats symptom reproduction as proof of outflow obstruction.

answerChoices.label: Reduced contraction reserve with impaired liquid-load outflow
answerChoices.rationale: This recognizes the reserve finding but overinterprets the familiar symptom despite the actual liquid-load pressure response.

answerChoices.label: Preserved contraction reserve with preserved liquid-load outflow
answerChoices.rationale: This correctly limits the outflow conclusion but confuses inhibition during the sequence with augmentation afterwards.

decisionNodes.explanation: Assess the recovery contraction separately from inhibition during rapid swallowing. Both repeats lack augmentation relative to baseline, supporting reduced reserve. Junction relaxation and the absence of a body pressure column during drinking do not support impaired liquid-load outflow merely because discomfort occurs. These challenge observations do not assign the final motor diagnosis or explain every symptom.

exhibit.caption: Constructed pressure-study schematic; qualitative teaching observations, not a patient recording.
exhibit.description: Panel A shows a propagated baseline esophageal-body contraction. In both rapid-swallow repeats, body pressure falls during the sequence and the contraction afterwards is smaller than the baseline contraction. During the rapid-drink panel the junction relaxes within the laboratory range and no body-wide pressure column develops. The familiar discomfort occurs during that drink.

answerChoices.label: Supervised oxycodone adjustment with repeat manometry
answerChoices.rationale: The interval exposure can produce a spastic/outflow pattern; assessing its reversibility changes whether the current result should drive irreversible treatment.

answerChoices.label: Timed barium esophagography during the current oxycodone regimen
answerChoices.rationale: This can assess bolus passage, but persistence of a finding during the same exposure does not resolve whether it is medication-associated and reversible.

answerChoices.label: Junction distensibility testing during the current oxycodone regimen
answerChoices.rationale: This may add useful supportive physiology, but does not first remove the represented potentially reversible exposure.

decisionNodes.explanation: The current study should not be read without the interval medication record. Oxycodone was introduced between different pressure studies and was taken before the abnormal one. Opioid-associated patterns can resemble spastic junction disorders; when feasible, supervised medication adjustment followed by repeat assessment can change the basis for an irreversible treatment. Do not abruptly stop prescribed opioids. Additional transit or distensibility testing may still be needed; the case does not diagnose primary achalasia or prescribe an interruption interval.

case.displayName: Matching esophageal provocation to unexplained food symptoms
case.presentation: {patientName}, a 52-year-old man, attends clinic with episodes in which rice or meat stops behind the sternum. Endoscopy has assessed the lumen and mucosa without finding a fixed narrowing or explanatory lesion. The motility team is deciding what the existing pressure responses establish and which acquisition should precede a junction-directed treatment decision.

decisionNodes.stem: Which report interpretation and next protocol should be sent to {patientName}'s motility team?

answerChoices.label: Reduced post-sequence reserve with standardized-meal manometry
answerChoices.rationale: The rapid-swallow result concerns post-sequence augmentation rather than failed inhibition. It does not explain the patient's food episodes, for which the remaining symptom-matched meal study can add information.

answerChoices.label: Reduced swallowing inhibition with standardized-meal manometry
answerChoices.rationale: A meal may address the residual symptom, but pressure does fall during the rapid sequence; the abnormality is after the sequence rather than inhibition during it.

answerChoices.label: Reduced post-sequence reserve with rapid-drink liquid manometry
answerChoices.rationale: This reads reserve correctly but repeats the liquid-loading question already addressed without targeting the remaining food-associated episodes.

answerChoices.label: Reduced swallowing inhibition with rapid-drink liquid manometry
answerChoices.rationale: This misreads the phase of the rapid-swallow response and redirects acquisition to the already assessed liquid-loading question.

decisionNodes.explanation: Separate what happens during a rapid-swallow sequence from what follows it. Pressure suppression during the sequence is present; augmentation afterward is not. That reserve result is different from liquid-loading outflow assessment, and neither provides a symptom-matched food challenge here. Correct the report and obtain standardized-meal manometry before using the unexplained episodes to select an irreversible junction treatment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which physiologic investigation should be obtained next for {patientName}'s persistent swallowing symptoms?

answerChoices.label: High-resolution manometry with positional pressure assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Defines junction relaxation and esophageal-body motor patterns after the supplied structural evaluation.

answerChoices.label: Functional lumen imaging with endoscopic distension assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Provides useful complementary distensibility information but does not replace the primary pressure-based classification study in this ordinary workup.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory pH-impedance monitoring with symptom association assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Investigates a reflux hypothesis rather than establishing the motor pattern responsible for the combined swallowing observations.

decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation and planning decision should follow {patientName}'s study?

answerChoices.label: Conclusive achalasia pattern; arrange junction-directed treatment assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Complete failed peristalsis with abnormal primary-position relaxation pressure meets the classification despite a normal secondary-position pressure.

answerChoices.label: Inconclusive outflow-obstruction pattern; obtain corroboration before treatment assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Overapplies the both-position EGJOO requirement to a patient with no preserved peristalsis.

answerChoices.label: Absent-contractility pattern; arrange reflux-directed management assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Treats the normal upright measurement as overriding the abnormal adequate primary-position study.

decisionNodes.explanation: All primary-position swallows fail and junction relaxation pressure is abnormal in that adequate series. A normal upright pressure does not impose the both-position EGJOO rule on this achalasia pattern. Arrange specialist treatment assessment rather than classifying the study as absent contractility or automatically inconclusive EGJOO.

decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation and planning decision should follow {patientName}'s study?

answerChoices.label: Conclusive achalasia pattern; arrange junction-directed treatment assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Complete failed peristalsis with abnormal primary-position relaxation pressure meets the classification despite a normal secondary-position pressure.

answerChoices.label: Inconclusive outflow-obstruction pattern; obtain corroboration before treatment assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Overapplies the both-position EGJOO requirement to a patient with no preserved peristalsis.

answerChoices.label: Absent-contractility pattern; arrange reflux-directed management assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Treats the normal upright measurement as overriding the abnormal adequate primary-position study.

decisionNodes.explanation: All primary-position swallows fail and junction relaxation pressure is abnormal in that adequate series. A normal upright pressure does not impose the both-position EGJOO rule on this achalasia pattern. Arrange specialist treatment assessment rather than classifying the study as absent contractility or automatically inconclusive EGJOO.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: All primary-position swallows fail and junction relaxation pressure is abnormal in that adequate series. Coordinate a clinically appropriate withdrawal/reassessment plan before treating this as established primary disease requiring myotomy. No abrupt cessation or fixed washout is prescribed.

answerChoices.label: Manometry with endoscopic catheter placement
answerChoices.rationale: Without gastric/junction recordings the tracing cannot establish relaxation or subtype; assisted completion is available before abandoning manometry.

answerChoices.label: Obtain junction distensibility measurements with endoscopic FLIP
answerChoices.rationale: FLIP can complement an obstructive-symptom assessment, especially when manometry cannot be completed despite assisted placement, but does not replace the still-feasible pressure classification required here.

answerChoices.label: Obtain a timed barium esophagram with a tablet
answerChoices.rationale: Timed barium emptying helps assess obstruction but does not supply the missing junction-relaxation and peristaltic classification measurements.

decisionNodes.explanation: Recognize that the catheter never sampled below the junction, so pressurization is not a valid subtype classification. Select assisted completion rather than treating an uninterpretable study. Manometry classification requires a technically adequate acquisition. Complementary tests do not make a missing pressure measurement valid; protocols should answer the particular unresolved question.

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should resolve {patientName}'s pressure-study findings?

answerChoices.label: Manometry with endoscopic catheter placement
answerChoices.rationale: Without gastric/junction recordings the tracing cannot establish relaxation or subtype; assisted completion is available before abandoning manometry.

answerChoices.label: Obtain junction distensibility measurements with endoscopic FLIP
answerChoices.rationale: FLIP can complement an obstructive-symptom assessment, especially when manometry cannot be completed despite assisted placement, but does not replace the still-feasible pressure classification required here.

answerChoices.label: Obtain a timed barium esophagram with a tablet
answerChoices.rationale: Timed barium emptying helps assess obstruction but does not supply the missing junction-relaxation and peristaltic classification measurements.

decisionNodes.explanation: Recognize that the catheter never sampled below the junction, so pressurization is not a valid subtype classification. answerChoices.label: Pressure recording during a standardized solid test meal
answerChoices.rationale: A solid-meal challenge can assess intermittent food-related obstructive physiology not represented by routine water swallows.

answerChoices.label: Pressure recording during a multiple rapid-swallow sequence
answerChoices.rationale: Rapid swallows assess inhibition and contractile reserve; that is a different question from the solid-food symptom challenge.

answerChoices.label: Pressure recording during an upright rapid-drink challenge
answerChoices.rationale: A liquid-load challenge can assess outflow, but does not reproduce the bolus conditions documented in this patient's diary.

decisionNodes.explanation: Provocative manometry should answer the unresolved physiological question. Here the routine water-swallow findings and structural/mucosal assessment leave meal-related obstructive symptoms unexplained. A standardized solid meal can relate symptoms to pressure behavior; rapid-swallow reserve and rapid-drink outflow maneuvers address different physiological questions.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Separated swallows produce propagated contractions with junction relaxation within the laboratory range. During repeated rapid-swallow sequences, body pressure falls while swallowing; the contraction after each sequence is weaker than the patient's baseline contractions. During upright rapid drinking, junction relaxation remains within the laboratory range and pressure does not build up throughout the esophagus.
decisionNodes.stem: Which interpretation should accompany {patientName}'s referral for specialist manometry review?

answerChoices.label: Reduced contractile reserve; liquid-load outflow obstruction not demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: The diminished post-sequence contraction concerns reserve, whereas the liquid-load response does not demonstrate an outflow obstruction. These are different physiology questions; neither finding alone supplies a complete motor diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Preserved contractile reserve; liquid-load outflow obstruction not demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: Normal suppression during rapid swallows concerns inhibition. It does not make the weaker post-sequence contraction evidence of preserved reserve.

answerChoices.label: Reduced contractile reserve; liquid-load outflow obstruction demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: The reserve interpretation fits, but the supplied junction relaxation and pressure behavior during rapid drinking do not establish the added outflow claim.

answerChoices.label: Preserved contractile reserve; liquid-load outflow obstruction demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: This confuses inhibition with reserve and interprets the liquid-load response as evidence of obstruction despite the stated observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: The response during rapid swallows and the contraction afterward answer different questions. Suppression is present, but the post-sequence response does not augment baseline contractions, supporting reduced reserve. The supplied rapid-drink response does not demonstrate outflow obstruction. Specialist review must integrate technically adequate acquisition and the full clinical context; these observations do not independently diagnose achalasia or establish the cause of all symptoms.

decisionNodes.stem: Which motility diagnosis best accounts for {patientName}'s returned study?

decisionNodes.explanation: The current study should not be read without the interval medication record. Oxycodone was introduced between different pressure studies and was taken before the abnormal one. Opioid-associated patterns can resemble spastic junction disorders; when feasible, supervised medication adjustment followed by repeat assessment can change the basis for an irreversible treatment. Do not abruptly stop prescribed opioids. Additional transit or distensibility testing may still be needed; the case does not diagnose primary achalasia or prescribe an interruption interval.

answerChoices.rationale: A tailored surgical myotomy can address the spastic segment and remains an accepted option. With comparable proposed coverage, the current observations do not establish why it must rank below POEM for this individual.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic graded pneumatic dilation of the junction
answerChoices.rationale: Dilation is a definitive option in selected achalasia patients, but treating junction resistance with a balloon does not address the demonstrated spastic body extent as a tailored myotomy can.

answerChoices.label: Peroral endoscopic myotomy across the involved segment
answerChoices.rationale: The raw findings support a spastic achalasia phenotype and a tailored myotomy. SAGES favors POEM by expert opinion, but this alone does not settle the offered comparison with a comparably tailored Heller plan in an unapproved teaching item.

decisionNodes.explanation: The pressure and body-timing observations support a spastic achalasia phenotype. A myotomy addressing the involved body segment is preferable to treating only the junction with dilation. The offered POEM-versus-tailored-Heller ranking remains unresolved for this constructed patient; the item is parked and its provisional key is not authorized for scoring.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should next assess {patientName}'s recurrent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The later record documents POEM followed by a period of comfortable eating. Food now pauses and fluid returns at night. The completed repeat manometry has adequate junction-crossing positional acquisition, relaxation within the laboratory interval and no residual premature contractions. Her weight and oral hydration are maintained.

answerChoices.label: Upper endoscopy with esophageal and junction inspection
answerChoices.rationale: Endoscopy can identify reflux injury or a post-treatment narrowing and may be complementary in the full reassessment. For this stable recurrent food-and-fluid hold-up, timed barium is the guideline-supported first objective test of emptying; the reassuring pressure study has not answered that question.

answerChoices.label: Upright timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
answerChoices.rationale: Normal measured relaxation and absence of residual spasm do not establish bolus emptying. Upright timed barium testing directly assesses clearance and is the ACG first-line objective investigation for recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia treatment.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Nocturnal fluid return after POEM makes reflux a credible mechanism. Her recurrent food hold-up still requires objective clearance assessment first; reflux monitoring answers a different question once clearance and structural findings have been considered.

decisionNodes.explanation: Improved pressure relaxation does not show that swallowed material leaves the esophagus. Recurrent food hold-up after POEM warrants timed barium assessment first. Endoscopy can examine injury or narrowing, and reflux monitoring can resolve an outstanding reflux question; neither replaces the present emptying assessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which medication plan should next address {patientName}'s persistent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent upright timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Endoscopy shows distal mucosal breaks, without retained food or a fixed narrowing. She describes burning and sour fluid return, especially after lying down. Bottle review confirms conventional delayed-release omeprazole taken every day at bedtime, several hours after dinner.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole daily before breakfast
answerChoices.rationale: The clearance and mucosal findings support a reflux-injury target. Daily conventional delayed-release omeprazole has been taken away from a meal. Optimize its administration before judging that regimen insufficient or adding therapy.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole before breakfast and before dinner
answerChoices.rationale: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.

answerChoices.label: Use daily prebreakfast omeprazole with as-needed bedtime famotidine
answerChoices.rationale: Famotidine provides H2-receptor acid suppression, and selected patients have a role for as-needed bedtime H2 blockade for nocturnal symptoms during optimized PPI use. Adding it while first correcting PPI administration escalates treatment before the response to that correction is known.

decisionNodes.explanation: Prompt passage with distal mucosal injury shifts the present target toward reflux rather than another junction procedure. Daily pill taking does not establish an optimized conventional PPI regimen: move the daily omeprazole to before breakfast before escalating. Persistent disease after an adequate optimized course would justify reconsidering treatment intensity; selected nocturnal breakthrough has a different add-on pathway.

conceptVersion.learningObjective: Integrate a spastic achalasia pattern and its body extent when selecting an initial definitive procedure.
conceptVersion.identityReason: The older construct distinguishes a definitive procedure from reflux or palliative drugs. This successor compares definitive procedures using subtype and the spastic body segment.
conceptVersion.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

authorGate.parkReason: Removing the unique tailored qualifier and representing comparable body-plus-junction myotomy coverage leaves a legitimate tailored Heller alternative. Current SAGES preference is expert opinion, while ACG accepts tailored POEM or Heller. The represented anatomy does not independently establish a unique patient-specific ranking; do not invent a coverage cutoff or local permission to select POEM.

decisionNodes.stem: Which medication plan should next address {patientName}'s persistent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent upright timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Endoscopy shows distal mucosal breaks, without retained food or a fixed narrowing. She describes burning and sour fluid return, especially after lying down. Bottle review confirms conventional delayed-release omeprazole taken every day at bedtime, several hours after dinner.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole daily before breakfast
answerChoices.rationale: The clearance and mucosal findings support a reflux-injury target. Daily conventional delayed-release omeprazole has been taken away from a meal. Optimize its administration before judging that regimen insufficient or adding therapy.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole before breakfast and before dinner
answerChoices.rationale: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.

answerChoices.label: Use daily prebreakfast omeprazole with as-needed bedtime famotidine
answerChoices.rationale: Famotidine provides H2-receptor acid suppression, and selected patients have a role for as-needed bedtime H2 blockade for nocturnal symptoms during optimized PPI use. Adding it while first correcting PPI administration escalates treatment before the response to that correction is known.

authorGate.interpret: Separate an adequate normal post-treatment relaxation measurement from the unmeasured clearance of food and liquid.
authorGate.apply: Choose first-line objective emptying assessment for recurrent post-treatment swallowing symptoms while retaining mucosal injury and reflux as genuine alternatives.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Recurrent food hold-up persists after an adequate pressure study, while no new objective clearance result is available.
authorGate.counterfactual: If a completed timed study instead showed satisfactory passage and the outstanding problem was a suspected mucosal lesion or luminal narrowing, upper endoscopy would become the appropriate offered investigation.
authorGate.deletionTest: The completed POEM establishes the treatment phase. Food hold-up identifies the unresolved functional problem. Normal acquired pressure data test whether the learner confuses relaxation with emptying. Maintained intake keeps this an outpatient diagnostic choice.
authorGate.cueAttack: Every label names a distinct investigation. None repeats a just-completed study. The task names symptoms rather than a clearance target, and the key is not the only new option. Endoscopy remains legitimate complementary care but is ranked after first-line emptying assessment here.
authorGate.stageAudit: Three diagnostic investigations before an additional treatment decision. No present procedure competes against an information-gathering key.
authorGate.difficultyReason: The resident must avoid overinterpreting reassuring manometry and rank complementary tests for recurrent obstructive symptoms. This is a fair moderate application, not a claim of independently hard performance.
authorGate.sequenceAudit: First active node in this case. It explicitly restates actual POEM and its response. Its feedback does not supply subsequent clearance findings, mucosal findings or the medication decision.
authorGate.remainingRisk: Endoscopy is complementary and may be ordered during a complete assessment. Melissa must confirm the first-investigation ranking for this stable presentation. Exact candidate v2 needs independent and clinical review.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial procedure is best supported by {patientName}'s evaluation?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Her initial record documents progressive food-and-liquid dysphagia with swallowing-related pain. Endoscopy and cross-sectional assessment show no junction lesion. She uses no opioids. The anesthesia assessment permits either myotomy. The foregut proposals describe muscle division across the involved esophageal-body segment and junction for both myotomy approaches.

answerChoices.label: Laparoscopic Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication
answerChoices.rationale: A tailored surgical myotomy can address the spastic segment and remains an accepted option. With comparable proposed coverage, the current observations do not establish why it must rank below POEM for this individual.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic graded pneumatic dilation of the junction
answerChoices.rationale: Dilation is a definitive option in selected achalasia patients, but treating junction resistance with a balloon does not address the demonstrated spastic body extent as a tailored myotomy can.

answerChoices.label: Peroral endoscopic myotomy across the involved segment
answerChoices.rationale: The raw findings support a spastic achalasia phenotype and a tailored myotomy. SAGES favors POEM by expert opinion, but this alone does not settle the offered comparison with a comparably tailored Heller plan in an unapproved teaching item.

decisionNodes.explanation: The pressure and body-timing observations support a spastic achalasia phenotype. A myotomy addressing the involved body segment is preferable to treating only the junction with dilation. The offered POEM-versus-tailored-Heller ranking remains unresolved for this constructed patient; the item is parked and its provisional key is not authorized for scoring.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should next assess {patientName}'s recurrent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The later record documents POEM followed by a period of comfortable eating. Food now pauses and fluid returns at night. The completed repeat manometry has adequate junction-crossing positional acquisition, relaxation within the laboratory interval and no residual premature contractions. Her weight and oral hydration are maintained.

answerChoices.label: Upper endoscopy with esophageal and junction inspection
answerChoices.rationale: Endoscopy can identify reflux injury or a post-treatment narrowing and may be complementary in the full reassessment. For this stable recurrent food-and-fluid hold-up, timed barium is the guideline-supported first objective test of emptying; the reassuring pressure study has not answered that question.

answerChoices.label: Upright timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
answerChoices.rationale: Normal measured relaxation and absence of residual spasm do not establish bolus emptying. Upright timed barium testing directly assesses clearance and is the ACG first-line objective investigation for recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia treatment.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Nocturnal fluid return after POEM makes reflux a credible mechanism. Her recurrent food hold-up still requires objective clearance assessment first; reflux monitoring answers a different question once clearance and structural findings have been considered.

decisionNodes.explanation: Improved pressure relaxation does not show that swallowed material leaves the esophagus. Recurrent food hold-up after POEM warrants timed barium assessment first. Endoscopy can examine injury or narrowing, and reflux monitoring can resolve an outstanding reflux question; neither replaces the present emptying assessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which medication plan should next address {patientName}'s persistent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent upright timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Endoscopy shows distal mucosal breaks, without retained food or a fixed narrowing. She describes burning and sour fluid return, especially after lying down. Bottle review confirms conventional delayed-release omeprazole taken every day at bedtime, several hours after dinner.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole daily before breakfast
answerChoices.rationale: The clearance and mucosal findings support a reflux-injury target. Daily conventional delayed-release omeprazole has been taken away from a meal. Optimize its administration before judging that regimen insufficient or adding therapy.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole before breakfast and before dinner
answerChoices.rationale: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.

answerChoices.label: Use daily prebreakfast omeprazole with as-needed bedtime famotidine
answerChoices.rationale: Famotidine provides H2-receptor acid suppression, and selected patients have a role for as-needed bedtime H2 blockade for nocturnal symptoms during optimized PPI use. Adding it while first correcting PPI administration escalates treatment before the response to that correction is known.

decisionNodes.explanation: Prompt passage with distal mucosal injury shifts the present target toward reflux rather than another junction procedure. Daily pill taking does not establish an optimized conventional PPI regimen: move the daily omeprazole to before breakfast before escalating. Persistent disease after an adequate optimized course would justify reconsidering treatment intensity; selected nocturnal breakthrough has a different add-on pathway.

conceptVersion.learningObjective: Interpret post-myotomy clearance and mucosal observations, then optimize conventional PPI administration before escalating reflux therapy.
conceptVersion.identityReason: The reviewed v1 chooses initial acid suppression over unsupported repeat junction procedures. This version adds a distinct medication-use decision: optimize an actually acquired daily PPI administration pattern before escalation. Preserve v1 and its history separately.
conceptVersion.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

authorGate.interpret: Integrate actual liquid/tablet passage and distal mucosal breaks as evidence of a reflux-injury target after myotomy, rather than infer obstruction from recurrent symptoms.
authorGate.apply: Inspect actual conventional PPI use and optimize administration before escalating an untested daily regimen.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Every current daily dose is taken at bedtime hours after dinner; an optimized premeal daily regimen has not been tried.
authorGate.counterfactual: If an adequate course of correctly administered daily premeal omeprazole had already been completed with persistent reflux disease, the offered before-breakfast-and-dinner regimen would become a reasonable next plan.
authorGate.deletionTest: Clearance and mucosal observations identify the mechanism. Current formulation and actual use distinguish optimization from escalation. Recumbent symptoms make nighttime H2 blockade a credible temptation. Removing actual administration makes the medication comparison underdetermined.
authorGate.cueAttack: Three named medicine regimens replace the prior medicine-versus-unsupported-procedures set. Raw mucosal findings replace the supplied diagnosis. Comparable option lengths and repeated omeprazole avoid a sole-new-medicine key. The history states use without telling the learner it is inadequate.
authorGate.stageAudit: Three current reflux-medication regimens after objective reassessment, with monitoring common to every plan.
authorGate.difficultyReason: Requires mechanism interpretation followed by distinguishing medication administration from medication failure. Bedtime symptoms make escalation or H2 addition tempting. This is a fair moderate clinical application, not a measured or guaranteed hard item.
authorGate.sequenceAudit: Second active node. The first node discusses investigations but neither names a PPI nor teaches medication scheduling. All decisive clearance, mucosal and medication observations appear only in this update, which also states the actual POEM timepoint.
authorGate.remainingRisk: New medication-use meaning requires a new concept version and independent/clinical review. General ACG GERD guidance directly supports optimization; one adequate guideline supplies this step. Coordinate ownership with the GERD lane. No invented dose, failure interval, injury grade or procedure threshold is used.

optionAudit.temptation: This requires using the actual administration record rather than equating daily pill use with optimized acid suppression.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: The clearance and mucosal findings support a reflux-injury target. Daily conventional delayed-release omeprazole has been taken away from a meal. Optimize its administration before judging that regimen insufficient or adding therapy.
optionAudit.correctUnder: A conventional daily PPI has not been used before the first meal and persistent reflux symptoms are being reassessed.

optionAudit.temptation: Interpret symptoms despite daily pill taking as failure of optimized daily PPI treatment and escalate immediately.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Persistent reflux disease remains after an adequate trial of correctly administered daily PPI, and the treating clinician selects premeal twice-daily therapy.

optionAudit.temptation: Let the nocturnal symptom timing select an added nighttime medicine without examining how the existing PPI is used.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Famotidine provides H2-receptor acid suppression, and selected patients have a role for as-needed bedtime H2 blockade for nocturnal symptoms during optimized PPI use. Adding it while first correcting PPI administration escalates treatment before the response to that correction is known.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Selected nocturnal symptoms or demonstrated nocturnal acid breakthrough persist despite an optimized daily premeal PPI regimen.

answerChoices.label: Upper endoscopy with esophageal and junction inspection
answerChoices.rationale: Endoscopy can identify reflux injury or a post-treatment narrowing and may be complementary in the full reassessment. answerChoices.label: Upright timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
answerChoices.rationale: Normal measured relaxation and absence of residual spasm do not establish bolus emptying. Upright timed barium testing directly assesses clearance and is the ACG first-line objective investigation for recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia treatment.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Nocturnal fluid return after POEM makes reflux a credible mechanism. Her recurrent food hold-up still requires objective clearance assessment first; reflux monitoring answers a different question once clearance and structural findings have been considered.

decisionNodes.stem: Which medication plan should next address {patientName}'s persistent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent upright timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Bottle review confirms conventional delayed-release omeprazole taken every day at bedtime, several hours after dinner.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole daily before breakfast
answerChoices.rationale: The clearance and mucosal findings support a reflux-injury target. Daily conventional delayed-release omeprazole has been taken away from a meal. Optimize its administration before judging that regimen insufficient or adding therapy.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole before breakfast and before dinner
answerChoices.rationale: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.

answerChoices.label: Use daily prebreakfast omeprazole with as-needed bedtime famotidine
