conceptVersion.learningObjective: Distinguish a retained-peristalsis pressure pattern from conclusive achalasia and choose a complementary obstruction assessment.
conceptVersion.identityReason: Existing EGJOO appears as a diagnostic foil. This new construct scores the additional evidence needed to establish its clinical relevance.
conceptVersion.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

authorGate.interpret: Recognize a manometric outflow-obstruction pattern with preserved peristalsis rather than label all elevated relaxation pressures achalasia.
authorGate.apply: Seek independent supportive obstruction evidence before choosing treatment, rather than adding pressure observations to an already adequate symptomatic study.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The positional liquid study already shows the outflow pattern and reproduces symptoms, but no independent passage or distensibility result has corroborated obstruction.
authorGate.counterfactual: If liquid swallows and positional pressures were normal and did not explain symptoms confined to eating solid meals, the offered standardized solid-meal manometry extension would become reasonable.
authorGate.deletionTest: Retained propagation distinguishes this construct from conclusive achalasia. Positional pressure elevation, intrabolus pressure and symptom reproduction establish the adequate manometric pattern. Exposure and operation history prevent an unrepresented secondary explanation from deciding the item.
authorGate.cueAttack: The task names persistent dysphagia without naming the desired mechanism or treatment assessment. All choices are distinct plausible investigations; a genuine meal protocol replaces the advertised routine repeat. FLIP is deliberately absent because it is also an accepted corroborating method.
authorGate.stageAudit: Three investigations at the diagnostic confirmation stage, before junction treatment is selected.
authorGate.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting retained propagation with abnormal junction pressures and distinguishing supportive confirmation from meaningful but less decisive meal provocation. This fairly tests a specialized application of a high-value treatment-before-confirmation principle.
authorGate.sequenceAudit: Standalone. No preceding subtype label or explanation supplies the supportive-test decision.
authorGate.remainingRisk: Exact v2 diagnostic ranking remains subject to clinical and independent review. This retains the v1 clinical meaning and concept identity; no second accepted supportive modality is offered.

conceptVersion.learningObjective: Choose complementary distensibility assessment after genuine repeated inability to complete pressure testing.
conceptVersion.identityReason: The live acquisition questions favor assisted completion. This new boundary asks what to do after assistance has also failed to produce usable measurements.
conceptVersion.historyMigration: Retain prior definitions and histories on their existing identities.

authorGate.interpret: Separate demonstrated retention from unacquired pressure physiology, while weighing the actual structural workup and the course for a secondary junction process.
authorGate.apply: Choose complementary opening and motor-response assessment after true assisted-manometry failure rather than a wall-targeting or reflux-targeting study.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The assisted post-recovery series remains unusable, while the structural assessment has no focal wall finding and the course has no new weight-loss signal.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the cardia imaging instead showed new focal junction-wall thickening despite unrevealing mucosal examination, EUS would become the offered priority to investigate a secondary structural cause.
authorGate.deletionTest: Both actual acquisition episodes define the failed-assistance boundary. Retention establishes the unresolved obstructive physiology. The structural assessment and course distinguish an occult-wall workup. Removing those observations would make the EUS comparison less determined.
authorGate.cueAttack: All three investigations are new in this record and labels have comparable scope. None repeats a narrated failure. The task names no distensibility measurement. Selecting FLIP now requires knowing what each new investigation can resolve rather than selecting novelty.
authorGate.stageAudit: Three diagnostic investigations after documented acquisition failure, without a premature treatment alternative.
authorGate.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting the remaining diagnostic gap and choosing among physiologic, structural-wall and reflux pathways. This is advanced narrow motility coverage; high examination yield and independently hard performance are not claimed.
authorGate.sequenceAudit: Standalone and optional advanced coverage. It must not be paired immediately with another scored assisted-manometry repair of the same unresolved acquisition.
authorGate.remainingRisk: Normal structural assessment does not absolutely exclude an infiltrative process. Melissa must confirm the represented course makes FLIP the best offered next step. Upper-endoscopy timing is an existing placeholder for both FLIP and EUS; no new service executes in this sidecar.

optionAudit.temptation: Pursue a real occult structural mimic as the next explanation without weighing the existing structural record and the unresolved physiologic acquisition.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: An infiltrative junction process can mimic a motor disorder despite an unrevealing mucosal examination. EUS is useful when clinical or imaging findings raise that concern. The represented gradual, weight-stable course and prior structural assessment provide no new wall target; the outstanding gap is usable physiology after failed assisted manometry.
optionAudit.correctUnder: New focal junction-wall thickening or another substantial concern for an infiltrative lesion persists despite unrevealing mucosal inspection or sampling.

optionAudit.temptation: The key requires distinguishing failure to acquire pressure data from the supportive obstruction observations already available.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Retention has been documented but usable pressure physiology has not been acquired despite assisted placement. FLIP is a supported complementary assessment of junction opening and motor response in this circumstance. It neither supplies a complete manometric subtype nor by itself authorizes myotomy.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Obstructive symptoms persist and standard pressure testing remains incomplete despite assisted placement.

optionAudit.temptation: Treat regurgitation as evidence of reflux and select a reflux test before resolving the retained-bolus physiology.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Regurgitation can reflect reflux, but the acquired retained-column pattern and incomplete motor assessment leave obstructive physiology unresolved. Reflux burden and symptom association do not characterize that opening problem.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Clearance and structural causes have been adequately assessed and the remaining question is whether symptoms track abnormal reflux.

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan best fits {patientName}'s earlier referral after dilation and POEM had failed?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At that earlier referral she was fit for major surgery but continued to retain food after graded dilation and POEM. The timed study showed a relatively straight esophagus with hold-up at the junction. Endoscopy showed no reflux stricture or malignancy. Distensibility remained reduced, and review of the POEM report documented that the muscle division had stopped short of the gastric extension.

answerChoices.rationale: Temporary symptom relief is appropriate when definitive therapy is unsuitable. Her fitness and residual correctable target support considering definitive salvage here.

decisionNodes.stem: Which referral best fits {patientName}'s current outside-hospital findings?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The later records document completion of Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication and initial improvement. At her current admission she again regurgitated retained food and developed aspiration-related illness. After respiratory recovery, the esophagram showed a markedly dilated sigmoid esophagus with dependent pools persisting through the timed series. Endoscopy and FLIP showed a widely opening junction with no fixed stricture. The operative record confirms a completed myotomy. Nutrition and cardiopulmonary assessment support considering major surgery after optimization.

answerChoices.rationale: Further muscle division can treat an incomplete myotomy. The current record instead shows adequate junction opening and severe distorted-reservoir retention after completed therapies.

optionAudit.correctUnder: An individualized foregut assessment selects a tailored surgical myotomy with suitable coverage and reflux protection.

authorChecks.interpret: Separate an adequate normal post-treatment relaxation measurement from the unmeasured clearance of food and liquid.
authorChecks.apply: Choose first-line objective emptying assessment for recurrent post-treatment swallowing symptoms while retaining mucosal injury and reflux as genuine alternatives.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: Recurrent food hold-up persists after an adequate pressure study, while no new objective clearance result is available.
authorChecks.counterfactual: If a completed timed study instead showed satisfactory passage and the outstanding problem was a suspected mucosal lesion or luminal narrowing, upper endoscopy would become the appropriate offered investigation.
authorChecks.deletionTest: The completed POEM establishes the treatment phase. Food hold-up identifies the unresolved functional problem. Normal acquired pressure data test whether the learner confuses relaxation with emptying. Maintained intake keeps this an outpatient diagnostic choice.
authorChecks.cueAttack: Every label names a distinct investigation. None repeats a just-completed study. The task names symptoms rather than a clearance target, and the key is not the only new option. Endoscopy remains legitimate complementary care but is ranked after first-line emptying assessment here.
authorChecks.stageAudit: Three diagnostic investigations before an additional treatment decision. No present procedure competes against an information-gathering key.
authorChecks.difficultyReason: The resident must avoid overinterpreting reassuring manometry and rank complementary tests for recurrent obstructive symptoms. This is a fair moderate application, not a claim of independently hard performance.
authorChecks.sequenceAudit: First active node in this case. It explicitly restates actual POEM and its response. Its feedback does not supply subsequent clearance findings, mucosal findings or the medication decision.
authorChecks.remainingRisk: Endoscopy is complementary and may be ordered during a complete assessment. Melissa must confirm the first-investigation ranking for this stable presentation. Exact candidate v2 needs independent and clinical review.

optionAudit.temptation: Prioritize possible reflux injury or stricture after POEM before characterizing whether the esophagus empties.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Endoscopy can identify reflux injury or a post-treatment narrowing and may be complementary in the full reassessment. For this stable recurrent food-and-fluid hold-up, timed barium is the guideline-supported first objective test of emptying; the reassuring pressure study has not answered that question.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Objective clearance is satisfactory and a mucosal lesion or luminal narrowing remains the unresolved target of the symptom evaluation.

optionAudit.temptation: The key depends on recognizing that pressure relaxation and bolus clearance are different observations.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Normal measured relaxation and absence of residual spasm do not establish bolus emptying. Upright timed barium testing directly assesses clearance and is the ACG first-line objective investigation for recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia treatment.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Persistent or recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia therapy require objective emptying assessment.

optionAudit.temptation: Attribute nocturnal fluid return directly to reflux after POEM.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Nocturnal fluid return after POEM makes reflux a credible mechanism. Her recurrent food hold-up still requires objective clearance assessment first; reflux monitoring answers a different question once clearance and structural findings have been considered.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Clearance has been adequately assessed and the unresolved question is whether symptoms correlate with pathologic reflux.

authorChecks.interpret: Integrate actual liquid/tablet passage and distal mucosal breaks as evidence of a reflux-injury target after myotomy, rather than infer obstruction from recurrent symptoms.
authorChecks.apply: Inspect actual conventional PPI use and optimize administration before escalating an untested daily regimen.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: Every current daily dose is taken at bedtime hours after dinner; an optimized premeal daily regimen has not been tried.
authorChecks.counterfactual: If an adequate course of correctly administered daily premeal omeprazole had already been completed with persistent reflux disease, the offered before-breakfast-and-dinner regimen would become a reasonable next plan.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Clearance and mucosal observations identify the mechanism. Current formulation and actual use distinguish optimization from escalation. Recumbent symptoms make nighttime H2 blockade a credible temptation. Removing actual administration makes the medication comparison underdetermined.
authorChecks.cueAttack: Three named medicine regimens replace the prior medicine-versus-unsupported-procedures set. Raw mucosal findings replace the supplied diagnosis. Comparable option lengths and repeated omeprazole avoid a sole-new-medicine key. The history states use without telling the learner it is inadequate.
authorChecks.stageAudit: Three current reflux-medication regimens after objective reassessment, with monitoring common to every plan.
authorChecks.difficultyReason: Requires mechanism interpretation followed by distinguishing medication administration from medication failure. Bedtime symptoms make escalation or H2 addition tempting. This is a fair moderate clinical application, not a measured or guaranteed hard item.

General ACG GERD guidance directly supports optimization; one adequate guideline supplies this step. Coordinate ownership with the GERD lane. optionAudit.temptation: This requires using the actual administration record rather than equating daily pill use with optimized acid suppression.

optionAudit.correctUnder: A conventional daily PPI has not been used before the first meal and persistent reflux symptoms are being reassessed.

optionAudit.temptation: Interpret symptoms despite daily pill taking as failure of optimized daily PPI treatment and escalate immediately.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Persistent reflux disease remains after an adequate trial of correctly administered daily PPI, and the treating clinician selects premeal twice-daily therapy.

optionAudit.temptation: Let the nocturnal symptom timing select an added nighttime medicine without examining how the existing PPI is used.

Adding it while first correcting PPI administration escalates treatment before the response to that correction is known.

authorChecks.apply: Seek independent supportive obstruction evidence before choosing treatment, rather than adding pressure observations to an already adequate symptomatic study.

authorChecks.counterfactual: If liquid swallows and positional pressures were normal and did not explain symptoms confined to eating solid meals, the offered standardized solid-meal manometry extension would become reasonable.

Positional pressure elevation, intrabolus pressure and symptom reproduction establish the adequate manometric pattern. Exposure and operation history prevent an unrepresented secondary explanation from deciding the item.

All choices are distinct plausible investigations; a genuine meal protocol replaces the advertised routine repeat. FLIP is deliberately absent because it is also an accepted corroborating method.

This fairly tests a specialized application of a high-value treatment-before-confirmation principle.

optionAudit.temptation: Choose a meaningful symptom-provoking protocol but mistake more pressure observations for the needed complementary confirmation.

Here the adequate positional study already demonstrates a retained-peristalsis outflow pattern with reproduced symptoms. Independent supportive obstruction evidence, rather than additional pressure provocation, is needed to establish its clinical relevance.

optionAudit.temptation: Attribute regurgitation-like hold-up to reflux because some body contractions persist.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Reflux monitoring can address a reflux hypothesis, but it does not establish whether the current preserved-peristalsis outflow pattern impedes passage.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Obstructive physiology has been adequately assessed and the unresolved question concerns reflux burden or symptom association.

optionAudit.temptation: The key requires interpreting retained peristalsis and then seeking independent functional corroboration.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Elevated outflow pressure with retained peristalsis is not conclusive achalasia. Even with relevant symptoms, the manometric outflow-obstruction pattern needs accepted supportive evidence that passage is impaired. Timed barium with a tablet addresses that question before treatment is chosen.
optionAudit.correctUnder: A symptomatic manometric EGJOO pattern remains to be corroborated by an accepted supportive study.

authorChecks.interpret: Separate demonstrated retention from unacquired pressure physiology, while weighing the actual structural workup and the course for a secondary junction process.
authorChecks.apply: Choose complementary opening and motor-response assessment after true assisted-manometry failure rather than a wall-targeting or reflux-targeting study.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: The assisted post-recovery series remains unusable, while the structural assessment has no focal wall finding and the course has no new weight-loss signal.
authorChecks.counterfactual: If the cardia imaging instead showed new focal junction-wall thickening despite unrevealing mucosal examination, EUS would become the offered priority to investigate a secondary structural cause.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Both actual acquisition episodes define the failed-assistance boundary. Retention establishes the unresolved obstructive physiology. The structural assessment and course distinguish an occult-wall workup. Removing those observations would make the EUS comparison less determined.
authorChecks.cueAttack: All three investigations are new in this record and labels have comparable scope. None repeats a narrated failure. The task names no distensibility measurement. Selecting FLIP now requires knowing what each new investigation can resolve rather than selecting novelty.
authorChecks.stageAudit: Three diagnostic investigations after documented acquisition failure, without a premature treatment alternative.
authorChecks.difficultyReason: Requires interpreting the remaining diagnostic gap and choosing among physiologic, structural-wall and reflux pathways. This is advanced narrow motility coverage; high examination yield and independently hard performance are not claimed.
authorChecks.sequenceAudit: Standalone and optional advanced coverage. It must not be paired immediately with another scored assisted-manometry repair of the same unresolved acquisition.
authorChecks.remainingRisk: Normal structural assessment does not absolutely exclude an infiltrative process. Melissa must confirm the represented course makes FLIP the best offered next step. Upper-endoscopy timing is an existing placeholder for both FLIP and EUS; no new service executes in this sidecar.

optionAudit.temptation: Pursue a real occult structural mimic as the next explanation without weighing the existing structural record and the unresolved physiologic acquisition.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: An infiltrative junction process can mimic a motor disorder despite an unrevealing mucosal examination. EUS is useful when clinical or imaging findings raise that concern. The represented gradual, weight-stable course and prior structural assessment provide no new wall target; the outstanding gap is usable physiology after failed assisted manometry.
optionAudit.correctUnder: New focal junction-wall thickening or another substantial concern for an infiltrative lesion persists despite unrevealing mucosal inspection or sampling.

optionAudit.temptation: The key requires distinguishing failure to acquire pressure data from the supportive obstruction observations already available.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Retention has been documented but usable pressure physiology has not been acquired despite assisted placement. FLIP is a supported complementary assessment of junction opening and motor response in this circumstance. It neither supplies a complete manometric subtype nor by itself authorizes myotomy.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Obstructive symptoms persist and standard pressure testing remains incomplete despite assisted placement.

optionAudit.temptation: Treat regurgitation as evidence of reflux and select a reflux test before resolving the retained-bolus physiology.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Regurgitation can reflect reflux, but the acquired retained-column pattern and incomplete motor assessment leave obstructive physiology unresolved. Reflux burden and symptom association do not characterize that opening problem.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Clearance and structural causes have been adequately assessed and the remaining question is whether symptoms track abnormal reflux.

authorChecks.interpret: Recognize that all failed contractions plus an upper-limit relaxation value do not settle achalasia versus absent contractility.
authorChecks.apply: Select complementary passage assessment before allowing the printed normal flag to close the workup.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: Body failure is universal in an adequate study and relaxation is at the boundary in both positions.
authorChecks.counterfactual: If separated liquid swallows have normal propagation and relaxation but fail to reproduce solid-food episodes, a standardized-meal extension becomes the relevant offered next study.
authorChecks.deletionTest: The location within the normal interval matters. Universal failure distinguishes this from an unrevealing liquid series. Removing either observation changes the differential and next-study ranking.
authorChecks.cueAttack: All choices are specific investigations with estimates. The task has no normal-pressure exclusion language. FLIP is kept outside the answer set because it is another defensible supportive test.
authorChecks.stageAudit: Three additional investigations after a completed baseline physiology study.
authorChecks.difficultyReason: The credible error is treating a reference-interval flag as a sufficient exclusion and choosing another symptom-protocol or reflux pathway.
authorChecks.sequenceAudit: Standalone. This shares the barium test with the EGJOO item but the discriminator is upper-normal IRP with absent peristalsis rather than retained peristalsis with elevated pressure.
authorChecks.remainingRisk: Clinician review must confirm that the constructed upper-limit record supplies adequate uncertainty without a fabricated device-specific cutoff.

optionAudit.temptation: Treat dysphagia with a formally normal relaxation number as a symptom-provocation problem.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: A meal challenge is useful when an adequate liquid study leaves episodic food symptoms unexplained. This study already demonstrates universal body failure with unresolved junction opening, warranting complementary assessment.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Routine liquid acquisition is adequate and unrevealing while meal-associated symptoms remain unexplained.

optionAudit.temptation: The key requires recognizing uncertainty within the reference boundary rather than treating normal-range as complete exclusion.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: The failed body series with upper-limit relaxation values remains inconclusive for achalasia versus absent contractility. A supportive passage study can clarify the obstruction question.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Dysphagia and an inconclusive achalasia/absent-contractility pattern require supportive assessment.

optionAudit.temptation: Assign a reflux-associated hypomotility explanation as soon as the relaxation number is printed inside the reference interval.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: A reflex reflux workup would leave the unresolved emptying and junction-opening question unanswered in this presentation.
optionAudit.correctUnder: The obstruction question has been resolved and a reflux mechanism is the remaining specific diagnostic concern.

authorChecks.interpret: Identify a persistent correctable junction target instead of inferring irreversible end-stage failure from treatment count.
authorChecks.apply: Choose organ-preserving salvage assessment before esophagectomy in favorable anatomy.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: The esophagus is relatively straight and the prior division did not reach the gastric extension.
authorChecks.counterfactual: Severe sigmoid distortion with a patent, adequately myotomized junction and continuing disabling retention after completed therapies would shift the offered referral toward esophagectomy assessment.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Prior treatments establish salvage phase. Fitness distinguishes definitive from temporary therapy. Anatomy and incomplete myotomy supply the organ-preserving target. Deleting those findings leaves the treatment-count shortcut unresolved.
authorChecks.cueAttack: All three options are referrals for named treatments. The key has no uniquely cautious assessment qualifier. The actual operative record is necessary evidence rather than an author-written correctable-lesion label.
authorChecks.stageAudit: Three treatment referrals for an already characterized failed-treatment state.
authorChecks.difficultyReason: The resident must prioritize mechanism and anatomy over the number of prior failures while avoiding premature resection.
authorChecks.sequenceAudit: Earlier historical stage. The patient's current age and clinic context remain in the header. Feedback does not specify the later anatomy or a future esophagectomy answer.
authorChecks.remainingRisk: Evidence for exact salvage sequencing is low certainty. Redo POEM is also plausible in some patients and is not ranked against Heller in this option set.

optionAudit.temptation: Count two failed treatment families as automatic exhaustion of salvage.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Resection can be appropriate after exhausted treatment in severely distorted disease. Favorable anatomy and a documented incomplete myotomy leave an organ-preserving target at this earlier stage.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Severe distorted anatomy and disabling retention persist after adequate therapies, with no useful residual junction target.

optionAudit.temptation: The key depends on distinguishing a failed intervention from a fully treated but irreversibly dysfunctional reservoir.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: The record identifies an incomplete prior myotomy and anatomy conducive to salvage. Guidance supports considering Heller before resection in this setting.
optionAudit.correctUnder: A fit patient has favorable anatomy and residual obstruction from incomplete myotomy after failed dilation and POEM.

optionAudit.temptation: Avoid a major salvage decision by defaulting to the lower-burden palliative procedure.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Temporary symptom relief is appropriate when definitive therapy is unsuitable. Her fitness and residual correctable target support considering definitive salvage here.
optionAudit.correctUnder: The patient cannot undergo appropriate definitive treatment and symptom relief is the agreed objective.

authorChecks.parkReason: After repairing chronology and referral-label symmetry, both repeat outlet procedures still lack a target at the widely patent junction. Prior salvage feedback also scaffolds the reservoir-versus-outlet distinction. The supported facts do not supply a credible different remaining strategy with a defensible single-best ranking; retain the fair observations and park the easy comparison.
authorChecks.interpret: Distinguish persistent dependent retention in a severely distorted reservoir from residual obstruction at an incompletely treated junction.
authorChecks.apply: Select specialist esophagectomy assessment after adequate prior treatments and recovery sufficient to consider major surgery.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: The junction opens widely after a completed myotomy while substantial dependent retention and aspiration consequences persist.
authorChecks.counterfactual: A relatively straight esophagus with retained material above a poorly opening junction and documented incomplete division would restore an organ-preserving junction-salvage referral such as redo myotomy.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Completed treatment and actual opening establish the absence of the previous target. Distortion and retention identify reservoir failure. Aspiration establishes consequence. Recovery and fitness support considering major surgery. Removing the new update leaves the earlier salvage plan appropriate.
authorChecks.cueAttack: Specialist-center and assessment wording is now common to all referrals. The necessary patent-junction finding still disposes of both outlet interventions. That unresolved option-quality limitation is recorded as a park rather than concealed by parallel wording.
authorChecks.stageAudit: Three referral destinations after a completed current anatomic and physiologic reassessment.
authorChecks.difficultyReason: The reservoir-failure mechanism is important, but there is no credible residual competitor in this option set after the acquired patent-junction findings.
authorChecks.sequenceAudit: The previous PASS feedback contrasts favorable anatomy and incomplete myotomy with an exhausted organ. This later reversal is scaffolded application. The entire paired candidate case is withheld from active preview to retain the PASS node's exact serialization while its companion is parked.
authorChecks.remainingRisk: Parked. Future authoring needs a supported alternative remaining strategy and a clinician-confirmed discriminator. The present data do not justify manufacturing one.

optionAudit.temptation: Assume a recurrent symptom always indicates recurrent sphincter resistance.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Further muscle division can treat an incomplete myotomy. The current record instead shows adequate junction opening and severe distorted-reservoir retention after completed therapies.
optionAudit.correctUnder: Reassessment identifies an incomplete myotomy and an anatomic target suited to another junction procedure.

optionAudit.temptation: The key requires recognizing a changed mechanism after earlier organ-preserving salvage was appropriate.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Disabling retention, aspiration consequences, severe distortion and failure despite adequate junction treatment support specialized resection assessment. The referral does not predetermine the final operation.
optionAudit.correctUnder: A potentially fit patient has severe distorted anatomy and consequential retention after adequate prior therapies.

optionAudit.temptation: Choose another lower-burden junction treatment despite the absence of its demonstrated target.
optionAudit.whyRankedHere: Dilation can help recurrent junction resistance, but the current studies show a widely opening junction and a severely distorted retaining reservoir.
optionAudit.correctUnder: A fit patient has recurrent obstructive resistance at the junction and a foregut team selects dilation with rescue planning.

sourceLimitations: The AGA official page returned HTTP 403 and supplied no evidence.
Medication timing and sequencing have one directly checked guideline. The NCI reference independently verifies the named H2 antagonist class.
The revised medication objective crosses the GERD boundary and requires manager coordination.

claim.statement: High-resolution esophageal manometry is the confirmatory physiologic test when achalasia is suspected after structural obstruction and concerning pseudoachalasia have been appropriately excluded.
claim.limitation: The accepted guideline rates diagnostic evidence as low despite strong consensus. This claim does not prescribe subtype thresholds or a treatment algorithm.
claim.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent solids-and-liquids dysphagia and regurgitation after an adequate EGD excludes mechanical obstruction and concerning pseudoachalasia.

entries.title: Swallowing follow-up — procedure after opioid reassessment
clarityIssues: The exhibit labels its first column 'Junction relaxation' but describes it as above or within a reference interval. Name the measured relaxation pressure; more relaxation and a higher residual relaxation pressure do not mean the same thing.
The presentation names a junction-myotomy referral, whereas the first option specifies a planned POEM. Identify the proposed procedure consistently if that distinction is retained.

cues.phrase: He now eats his usual meals without hold-up or regurgitation.
cues.why: Complete symptomatic recovery makes the only defer-and-follow-up option readily selectable without interpreting the pressure table. Preserve the outcome for fairness, but recognize that the table currently adds little discrimination.

cues.phrase: Defer junction myotomy and arrange clinical follow-up
cues.why: This is the sole nonprocedural, cautious plan; both competitors disrupt the junction despite the explicitly resolved problem. The two active-treatment alternatives do not create two consequential reasoning steps.

fairness: Deferral is the defensible offered answer after symptom resolution and normalized adequate repeat physiology. The explanation appropriately limits the inference to this patient's response rather than promising universal opioid reversibility.
No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. This is an offline editorial assessment of candidate text, not refreshed source verification or Melissa Rowland's clinical approval.

The standalone task is complete, and the named patient's age, sex and short complaint are consistent. The important reversible-cause concept is high yield, but the current options reduce it to recovery followed by observation.
suggestions: Relabel the exhibit column as the actual pressure measure and align the planned procedure across presentation and options.

Rebuild the options around credible competing follow-up or treatment decisions after reassessment. If a more demanding case requires discordant symptom and physiologic findings, author and clinically review that new scenario rather than hiding the present recovery or inventing a threshold.
If the exact uncomplicated recovery scenario is retained, seek explicit acceptance as a basic medication-reassessment item instead of claiming two-step resident difficulty.

entries.title: Painful swallowing — initial procedure for a spastic pattern
clarityIssues: 'Premature activity extends well above the distal junction' conveys the intended extent but leaves the comparison with the offered Heller operation underspecified. The options do not describe comparable intended myotomy coverage.
The broad presentation about initial and subsequent records is understandable, but the initial consultation and later outside treatment should remain visibly separated.

cues.phrase: Tailored peroral endoscopic myotomy
cues.why: Only POEM receives the favorable qualifier 'Tailored'; Heller is presented without an equivalent scope description. This signals a patient-specific advantage before the learner has compared procedures.

fairness: The supplied pressure and propagation findings support recognizing a spastic achalasia pattern and then selecting a procedure capable of addressing its extent. These are two meaningful, high-yield steps.

POEM is a plausible preferred answer. However, the candidate explanation itself acknowledges tailored Heller as legitimate, while the stem permits both approaches and does not specify their planned coverage. A legitimate alternative is not automatically an equal best answer, but the exact superiority claim requires clinician confirmation; no confident clinical error is asserted here.

Do not turn an expert-opinion preference into an assertion that Heller is contraindicated or ineffective. The offline review cannot establish the current strength or exact scope of the cited preference.
The initial node stands alone. Its explanation does not disclose the subsequent timed-barium answer or acid-suppression answer.
suggestions: Use parallel procedure labels without giving only POEM a 'Tailored' qualifier.

Have the clinician confirm that the precise offered Heller and POEM plans have a defensible ranking for the represented body involvement. Clarify clinically supported coverage if needed, without inventing a length cutoff or merely adding a permission sentence that announces the answer.
Retain the explanation's uncertainty about alternative myotomy approaches, and explain the actual deciding advantage rather than relying on a society-name appeal.

entries.title: Painful swallowing — recurrent symptoms after POEM

cues.phrase: Repeat manometry shows junction relaxation within the laboratory interval and no residual premature contractions.
cues.why: This makes 'Repeat positional high-resolution esophageal manometry' a disposable repeat-test foil: no acquisition defect or interval change is supplied to justify repeating the just-completed investigation. Even a nonmedical reader can eliminate the duplicate.

fairness: Timed barium is the defensible offered next study for recurrent obstructive symptoms after treatment; a normal relaxation-pressure result does not establish adequate emptying. Reflux monitoring is a plausible competing mechanism, but the food hold-up supports assessing clearance first.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The moderate difficulty comes from interpreting symptoms despite reassuring pressure findings and choosing a complementary assessment; one of the three choices currently fails to contribute a credible error.

This follows the initial POEM decision coherently, explicitly restates the actual outside POEM and subsequent course, and can stand alone with its own presentation/update/task. Prior feedback does not name this investigation. Later barium findings must remain later, as they are in the candidate sequence.
suggestions: Replace the immediate repeat-manometry distractor with a distinct, clinically plausible investigation at this same stage, and ensure the revised case still ranks timed barium uniquely. Do not simply substitute another equally acceptable complementary test.
Explain why reflux monitoring is less useful as the first offered step for this symptom pattern, rather than discussing only the limitation of pressure measurement.
Keep the later clearance result out of this node's visible update. Runtime waits for every investigation require a separate integration check; they cannot be verified from the reviewed prose.

entries.title: Painful swallowing — treatment after the clearance reassessment

cues.phrase: distal erosive esophagitis
cues.why: The endoscopic interpretation supplies the treatment target. That can be appropriate for management, but this option set then asks only for its familiar initial medicine rather than a second consequential decision.

cues.phrase: is taking no acid-suppressive medicine
cues.why: This explicit treatment omission points directly toward the sole medication option. Combined with the diagnosis and prompt clearance, it leaves little inference.

cues.phrase: Start oral omeprazole and reassess symptoms
cues.why: It is the only medical/reassessment plan against two junction-disrupting procedures whose target the update has already excluded. The category and caution asymmetry favors it without a substantive comparison.

fairness: Omeprazole is the defensible offered initial treatment for the represented reflux injury. There is no demonstrated obstructive target for dilation or repeat myotomy. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The serial change from recurrent hold-up to documented clearance and reflux injury is coherent. The task explicitly says post-POEM and the update contains the decisive findings, so it can stand alone. The preceding explanation discusses emptying without disclosing omeprazole.
The high-yield distinction between post-treatment obstruction and reflux is present, but the interpreted diagnosis and excluded procedural competitors make this exact node easy rather than two-step.
suggestions: Retain the necessary clearance and treatment-history data, but compare genuinely plausible reflux-management actions at the same stage, with a supported patient-specific discriminator.

If testing obstruction versus reflux is the intended objective, use sufficiently specific observed findings and credible alternative mechanisms rather than supplying the conclusion and two procedures with no remaining target.
Do not manufacture difficulty by withholding initial acid-suppression status or adding unsupported dose, duration or severity thresholds.

entries.title: Meals sticking — procedure selection with prohibitive rescue risk
fairness: Botulinum toxin injection is the defensible offered answer. The resident must recognize a junction-relaxation disorder and then distinguish a brief endoscopic treatment from pneumatic dilation's potential need for operative rescue and POEM's anesthesia burden.

The anesthesia assessment is necessary decision-critical information, not an unfair feasibility cue: all three options are phrased as endoscopic procedures, and choosing among them requires knowing their different risks. Age alone cannot select the key.

Pneumatic dilation is a credible near-miss because it can appear to satisfy the brief-endoscopy constraint. The explicit rescue limitation resolves that alternative. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The standalone node has a named patient, consistent age/sex, short complaint and complete task. This is a high-yield treatment-selection principle; difficulty is a qualitative prediction, not measured performance. PASS is editorial and does not confer clinical approval.
suggestions: Optional feedback improvement: explicitly explain why possible perforation requiring operative rescue makes pneumatic dilation less appropriate here, and why POEM does not meet the anesthesia constraint. The current explanation identifies the categories of risk without teaching the closest error fully.

entries.title: Food sticking — supportive testing with preserved peristalsis
clarityIssues: 'Junction-treatment assessment' is less concrete than naming the current clinical decision: which investigation should determine whether the pressure finding represents clinically relevant obstruction before treatment. Avoid wording that itself supplies the required inference.

cues.phrase: Repeat the routine positional water-swallow manometry study
cues.why: The update already describes an adequate positional study. 'Repeat the routine' advertises a redundant action with no represented defect, reducing the choice set without medical interpretation.

fairness: Timed barium with a tablet is the defensible offered supportive investigation. Interpreting elevated relaxation pressure with preserved propagation, then seeking evidence of clinically relevant obstruction before intervention, constitutes two meaningful steps.

The explanation's statement that retained peristalsis does not establish achalasia is true but incomplete teaching for this pattern: the clinically relevant outflow-obstruction question should be distinguished from merely ruling out achalasia.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Reflux monitoring is less appropriate for the represented obstructive symptoms and pressure findings, while repeating the same adequate acquisition is a weak distractor.

The standalone node is internally consistent and has the required patient context. The treatment-before-confirmation principle is high yield, although the technical classification detail is more specialized.
suggestions: Replace the routine-repeat foil with a genuinely plausible next investigation or plan and recheck that no second accepted supportive modality becomes an equally correct answer.
Use a direct neutral task such as which investigation should next inform care for this patient's persistent dysphagia; let the observations establish the relevance of obstruction.

In feedback, explain why this manometric outflow pattern requires supportive clinical evidence and why the preserved peristalsis changes interpretation. Do not imply that any elevated pressure result is achalasia.

entries.title: Swallowing evaluation — assessment after failed assisted manometry

cues.phrase: Repeat endoscopically assisted high-resolution manometry
cues.why: The stem has just narrated failure of exactly this approach after successful placement, with no change that would make another attempt useful. It is a repeated unsuccessful action beside a novel test.

cues.phrase: Repeat timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
cues.why: The other distractor also begins 'Repeat' and repeats an already informative study. FLIP is the only new investigation; a reader can choose novelty without understanding its measurements.

fairness: FLIP is a defensible complementary assessment when adequate manometry cannot be obtained despite assistance. The explanation appropriately avoids claiming that it reproduces a complete manometric subtype or automatically authorizes irreversible treatment.

The prior timed examination does not specify tablet use, so a repeat with a tablet is not literally identical in every respect. Nevertheless, the option set and explanation treat it as a completed, uninformative comparison rather than identifying a meaningful residual question.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Clinical relevance is real, but this exact repeated-acquisition rescue scenario is narrower than a clearly common general-surgery board objective; highYield=false is a qualitative scope judgment, not a claim about exam frequency.
The standalone timeline and task are clear. The nominal adequacy assessment and test selection collapse to choosing the only untried test, so two consequential steps are not demonstrated.
suggestions: Keep the actual failed acquisition history, but compare equally new and clinically credible next approaches with a supported discriminator. Do not disguise repeats with synonyms.
Clarify the completed contrast protocol only if the presence or absence of tablet testing truly changes the next decision.
Consider merging this narrow technical fallback into a broader, more testable dysphagia assessment objective unless the owner explicitly wants advanced motility acquisition coverage.

entries.title: Meals taking longer — absent propagation with borderline relaxation pressure
fairness: Timed barium with a tablet is the defensible offered next study. The learner must resist treating the normal-range flag as exclusion of an outflow disorder, interpret universal failed contractions with borderline relaxation pressure, and select complementary emptying assessment.

Solid-meal manometry is a credible competing extension rather than a caricature or an identical completed test. Supportive obstruction assessment is preferable for the represented inconclusive pattern; the explanation does not claim meal provocation is universally useless.

The laboratory-relative description supplies the boundary without inventing a device-independent numerical cutoff. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; exact classification and ranking remain subject to clinician review.

No diagnosis label, unique favorable qualifier, convergence pattern or nonmedical wording shortcut identifies the key. The standalone task and patient context are complete. The principle of further assessment despite a borderline normal result is high yield. PASS is editorial, not clinical approval.
suggestions: Optional feedback improvement: explain specifically why a solid-meal extension is less decisive than a complementary emptying study in this all-failed, borderline-pressure pattern, and why reflux monitoring does not resolve the present question.
Preserve the distinction between a supportive test and a final diagnosis; do not add an unsupported numerical boundary.

entries.title: Foregut record review — salvage before resection
fairness: Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication is a defensible offered salvage referral. The combination of relatively favorable esophageal geometry, residual junction restriction and incomplete prior muscle division supports addressing a remaining outlet target before organ resection.

Esophagectomy is a credible near-miss after both dilation and POEM have failed. The resident must distinguish a correctable treatment deficit from irreversible reservoir failure; fitness for major surgery does not by itself select the most radical operation.

The description that division stopped short of the gastric extension is decisive clinical evidence rather than an unfair lexical match: none of the options simply repeats that phrase. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

Other salvage approaches may also warrant specialist consideration, but they are not offered; this does not invalidate the relative ranking here. The explanation properly frames Heller as a consideration rather than a universally mandatory rescue.

The historical referral is explicitly identified in both update and task, so it is not confused with the present post-aspiration visit. The node stands alone and sets up a distinct later reassessment. This is a high-yield salvage-versus-resection principle. PASS is editorial, not clinical approval.
suggestions: Optional presentation cleanup: replace the game-role phrase 'The founder reviews' with a direct description of reviewing the earlier and current records.
Keep the exact historical timepoint visible and preserve the explanation's conditional specialist framing. Do not generalize this answer to all patients with prior failed POEM.

entries.title: Foregut record review — later referral with a patent junction
clarityIssues: 'At her current admission' conflicts with the presentation's clinic visit after discharge. Use the most recent admission and distinguish that admission from the current outpatient review.

For standalone display, the current update states prior Heller but does not itself summarize the earlier dilation and POEM failures. Those matter to the exhaustion-of-treatment argument and should be concisely available without relying on a previous node.

cues.phrase: Refer to a high-volume center for esophagectomy assessment
cues.why: Only the intended answer includes a specialist-center qualifier and a cautious assessment rather than referral for a specific repeat intervention. The added qualification and specificity distinguish it from both competitors.

cues.phrase: a widely opening junction with no fixed stricture
cues.why: Both distractors propose another intervention at that same junction. The necessary finding directly disposes of both alternatives, so the final choice has no credible residual competitor. Keep the observation but improve the comparison.

fairness: Assessment for esophagectomy at an experienced center is the defensible offered answer given distorted esophageal geometry, persistent retention, aspiration, completed outlet treatment and potential surgical fitness after optimization. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The correct referral is for assessment after optimization, not automatic immediate resection, and the explanation appropriately says diameter or intervention count alone is insufficient.

The sequence coherently changes from incomplete myotomy to failure despite a patent junction. However, the preceding explanation already contrasts favorable anatomy/incomplete myotomy with an 'exhausted organ' and resection. That scaffolds the later reversal and lowers its independent difficulty.

Even viewed alone, the two repeat-junction procedures are weak competitors once the update establishes a widely patent junction. The high-yield concept is present, but the current comparison does not sustain two consequential steps.
suggestions: Repair the admission-versus-clinic chronology and include a compact prior-treatment summary for standalone use.
Make referral labels parallel in specificity and stage; specialist-center assessment should not be a uniquely favorable qualifier on the key.

Compare credible remaining management/referral strategies for the actual reservoir-failure problem, using supported findings to separate them. Do not retain two already-excluded outlet procedures merely to make a three-option set.

Re-review the entire two-node sequence after revision. If prior feedback still teaches the later discriminator, describe the later item as scaffolded application rather than claiming independent hard reasoning.

authorGate.interpret: Read the exposure-linked serial change while confirming that the two studies are comparable.
authorGate.apply: Use current symptom and physiologic recovery to withdraw an unsupported junction procedure.

authorGate.counterfactual: If symptoms persist and the adequate repeat remains premature/failed with impaired relaxation after the coordinated adjustment, POEM assessment becomes the best offered plan after corroboration.
authorGate.deletionTest: The taper record establishes the exposure change. Meal recovery supplies current function. Protocol comparability prevents attributing discordance to technical differences. Removing the repeat data leaves the referral unresolved.
authorGate.cueAttack: Removed the old task's irreversible-procedure phrase and the mirrored unchanged-opioid qualifier on distractors. All options now decide the same referral after a real completed response. The key names a concrete action, with no generic individualized-treatment label.

authorGate.difficultyReason: The error is anchoring on a prior spastic study despite changed exposure and current acquired recovery. The normal repeat cannot be ignored merely because the original referral was persuasive.

approvedInstantiationProfiles.presentation: {patientName}, a 45-year-old woman, attends clinic for review of her swallowing evaluation and subsequent outside foregut records.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial procedure is best supported by {patientName}'s evaluation?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Her initial record documents progressive food-and-liquid dysphagia with swallowing-related pain. Endoscopy and cross-sectional assessment show no junction lesion. She uses no opioids and the anesthesia evaluation permits either endoscopic or laparoscopic myotomy.

exhibit.caption: Constructed adequate positional manometry record
cells: Median relaxation pressure above this laboratory's reference interval in the primary and upright series
Most separated swallows generate contractions earlier than the laboratory lower latency reference. The remaining swallows fail.
No normal propagated sequence occurs. Premature activity extends well above the distal junction.

answerChoices.label: Laparoscopic Heller myotomy with Dor fundoplication
answerChoices.rationale: Surgical myotomy remains a legitimate option. The substantial spastic body component supports a tailored approach and the current SAGES panel favors POEM in this subtype.

answerChoices.label: Graded pneumatic dilation of the distal junction
answerChoices.rationale: Dilation is a definitive option in selected achalasia patients, but treating junction resistance with a balloon does not address the demonstrated spastic body extent as a tailored myotomy can.

answerChoices.label: Tailored peroral endoscopic myotomy
answerChoices.rationale: The adequate study has impaired relaxation and premature/failed responses without normal peristalsis. A tailored POEM can include the involved body segment and follows the current SAGES preference for type III.

decisionNodes.explanation: Impaired relaxation with premature or failed swallows and absent normal peristalsis supports a spastic achalasia pattern. The body extent makes a tailored myotomy consequential. SAGES favors POEM for this subtype by expert opinion. Tailored Heller myotomy remains a clinically legitimate alternative requiring individual assessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should next assess {patientName}'s recurrent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The later record documents POEM followed by a period of comfortable eating. Food now pauses and fluid returns at night. Repeat manometry shows junction relaxation within the laboratory interval and no residual premature contractions. Her weight and oral hydration are maintained.

answerChoices.label: Repeat positional high-resolution esophageal manometry
answerChoices.rationale: The adequate repeat pressure study has answered the residual spasm and relaxation questions. Another pressure study will not directly establish the degree of retained bolus.

answerChoices.label: Upright timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
answerChoices.rationale: The current uncertainty is actual clearance despite improved relaxation measurements. Timed barium testing is the guideline-supported first objective assessment of recurrent post-treatment symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Reflux is a real alternative after POEM. Clearance assessment should first characterize the food-and-fluid hold-up in this recurrent swallowing presentation, with reflux evaluation as indicated by the resulting assessment.

decisionNodes.explanation: A lower junction relaxation pressure does not establish emptying. Assess the recurrent symptoms with timed barium clearance and integrate the result with the rest of the foregut evaluation. This result is still pending at this point in the chart review.

decisionNodes.stem: Which treatment should now address {patientName}'s post-POEM symptoms?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Endoscopy shows distal erosive esophagitis, with no retained food or fixed narrowing. She reports burning and sour fluid return and is taking no acid-suppressive medicine.

answerChoices.label: Arrange pneumatic dilation of the junction
answerChoices.rationale: Symptoms after POEM can reflect residual outflow resistance, but the acquired clearance and endoscopic findings favor mucosal reflux injury in this record.

answerChoices.label: Start oral omeprazole and reassess symptoms

authorGate.interpret: Distinguish persistent dependent retention in a severely distorted reservoir from residual obstruction at an incompletely treated junction.
authorGate.apply: Select specialist esophagectomy assessment after adequate prior treatments and recovery sufficient to consider major surgery.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The junction opens widely after a completed myotomy while substantial dependent retention and aspiration consequences persist.
authorGate.counterfactual: A relatively straight esophagus with retained material above a poorly opening junction and documented incomplete division would restore an organ-preserving junction-salvage referral such as redo myotomy.
authorGate.deletionTest: Completed treatment and actual opening establish the absence of the previous target. Distortion and retention identify reservoir failure. Aspiration establishes consequence. Recovery and fitness support considering major surgery. Removing the new update leaves the earlier salvage plan appropriate.
authorGate.cueAttack: All labels are referrals for specific procedures, and all include a named target. No invented diameter threshold or end-stage diagnosis appears before choice. The key's high-volume wording is clinically necessary but is a possible specificity cue for independent review.
authorGate.stageAudit: Three referral destinations after a completed current anatomic and physiologic reassessment.
authorGate.difficultyReason: The resident must change direction from the previous organ-preserving answer when the current mechanism differs, while respecting the morbidity of resection.
authorGate.sequenceAudit: The prior explanation gives the earlier salvage rationale and does not name the later referral. Current widely opening junction and distorted retention are new. Delete them and the previous answer would remain appropriate.
authorGate.remainingRisk: Low-certainty individualized surgery. Melissa must confirm that the constructed observations support resection assessment and that current recovery is adequately represented. No acute hospital care is executed in clinic.

nodes.identityReason: The retained draft chooses the next acquisition during opioid exposure. This version interprets an acquired off-medication response and decides whether the existing myotomy referral remains supported.
nodes.objective: Use actual symptom and pressure changes after coordinated opioid adjustment when deciding whether to retain an achalasia myotomy plan.
nodes.task: What should happen to {patientName}'s proposed junction procedure after this reassessment?
nodes.currentUpdate: Endoscopy found no fixed narrowing or mucosal lesion. His pain team completed a supervised oxycodone taper and established a nonopioid pain plan. He now eats his usual meals without hold-up or regurgitation. Both pressure studies used the same laboratory, catheter system and adequate positional protocol.

cells: Above the laboratory reference interval

Within the laboratory reference interval in both positions

choices.label: Proceed with the planned peroral endoscopic myotomy
choices.rationale: The earlier record supported a spastic outflow phenotype during exposure. Resolution of symptoms and normalization on the adequate repeat study remove the current basis for that procedure.
choices.temptation: Treat the earlier abnormal study as proof of a permanent primary motor disorder.
choices.correctUnder: Persistent symptoms and adequately corroborated primary spastic achalasia remain after reversible contributions are addressed.

choices.label: Defer junction myotomy and arrange clinical follow-up
choices.rationale: The actual off-medication course and repeat physiology no longer support a junction-disrupting procedure. Reassess if swallowing symptoms return.
choices.temptation: The action requires integrating acquired function with the exposure-linked pressure change.
choices.correctUnder: Symptoms resolve and an adequate reassessment no longer demonstrates the physiology prompting treatment.

choices.label: Replace the myotomy referral with pneumatic dilation
choices.rationale: Choosing a different junction-disrupting procedure still assumes a persisting obstruction that the current record does not demonstrate.
choices.temptation: Preserve a procedural plan by selecting an apparently smaller intervention.
choices.correctUnder: Persistent symptomatic junction obstruction has been established and dilation is chosen after procedural and rescue-risk assessment.

nodes.explanation: The changed exposure, recovered swallowing and adequate repeat physiology support deferring the junction procedure. This individual response informs his current plan. It does not establish that every opioid-associated pressure pattern will normalize.

reasoning.interpret: Read the exposure-linked serial change while confirming that the two studies are comparable.
reasoning.apply: Use current symptom and physiologic recovery to withdraw an unsupported junction procedure.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Usual meals are tolerated and normal propagation and relaxation are now acquired off oxycodone.
reasoning.counterfactual: If symptoms persist and the adequate repeat remains premature/failed with impaired relaxation after the coordinated adjustment, POEM assessment becomes the best offered plan after corroboration.
reasoning.deletionTest: The taper record establishes the exposure change. Meal recovery supplies current function. Protocol comparability prevents attributing discordance to technical differences. Removing the repeat data leaves the referral unresolved.
reasoning.cueAttack: Removed the old task's irreversible-procedure phrase and the mirrored unchanged-opioid qualifier on distractors. All options now decide the same referral after a real completed response. The key names a concrete action, with no generic individualized-treatment label.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three present decisions about the existing junction procedure. No next-test option competes with a premature treatment.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The error is anchoring on a prior spastic study despite changed exposure and current acquired recovery. The normal repeat cannot be ignored merely because the original referral was persuasive.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Standalone. No preceding feedback supplies the medication-response decision.
reasoning.remainingRisk: The recorded N2 REVISE hold remains open on the old exact version. Melissa must confirm this changed-meaning response-based successor and its follow-up wording.
