nodes.identityReason: The older construct distinguishes a definitive procedure from reflux or palliative drugs. This successor compares definitive procedures using subtype and the spastic body segment.
nodes.objective: Integrate a spastic achalasia pattern and its body extent when selecting an initial definitive procedure.
nodes.task: Which initial procedure is best supported by {patientName}'s evaluation?
nodes.currentUpdate: Her initial record documents progressive food-and-liquid dysphagia with swallowing-related pain. Endoscopy and cross-sectional assessment show no junction lesion. She uses no opioids and the anesthesia evaluation permits either endoscopic or laparoscopic myotomy.

exhibit.caption: Constructed adequate positional manometry record
cells: Median relaxation pressure above this laboratory's reference interval in the primary and upright series
Most separated swallows generate contractions earlier than the laboratory lower latency reference. The remaining swallows fail.
No normal propagated sequence occurs. Premature activity extends well above the distal junction.

choices.label: Laparoscopic Heller myotomy with Dor fundoplication
choices.rationale: Surgical myotomy remains a legitimate option. The substantial spastic body component supports a tailored approach and the current SAGES panel favors POEM in this subtype.
choices.temptation: Choose the familiar surgical operation while underweighting the body extent and subtype-specific preference.
choices.correctUnder: A suitable type I/II patient chooses surgical myotomy, or an individualized foregut assessment favors a tailored surgical approach.

choices.label: Graded pneumatic dilation of the distal junction
choices.rationale: Dilation is a definitive option in selected achalasia patients, but treating junction resistance with a balloon does not address the demonstrated spastic body extent as a tailored myotomy can.
choices.temptation: Treat every achalasia phenotype as an isolated sphincter problem.
choices.correctUnder: A suitable patient with a nonspastic phenotype chooses dilation after discussion of repeat-treatment and rescue risks.

choices.label: Tailored peroral endoscopic myotomy
choices.rationale: The adequate study has impaired relaxation and premature/failed responses without normal peristalsis. A tailored POEM can include the involved body segment and follows the current SAGES preference for type III.
choices.temptation: The key requires interpreting both junction and body findings before applying the procedure preference.
choices.correctUnder: A suitable adult has a substantial spastic achalasia pattern and an experienced foregut team can plan tailored POEM.

nodes.explanation: Impaired relaxation with premature or failed swallows and absent normal peristalsis supports a spastic achalasia pattern. The body extent makes a tailored myotomy consequential. SAGES favors POEM for this subtype by expert opinion. Tailored Heller myotomy remains a clinically legitimate alternative requiring individual assessment.

reasoning.interpret: Separate premature activity plus impaired relaxation from distal spasm with normal relaxation or preserved-peristalsis EGJOO.
reasoning.apply: Use the substantial spastic body component and current subtype-specific guidance to compare definitive procedures.
reasoning.decidingObservation: The adequate study has no normal peristalsis and premature activity well above the junction.
reasoning.counterfactual: If a nonspastic pattern replaces the premature body activity, a surgically suitable patient choosing the surgical approach can appropriately receive Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication. POEM would lose its subtype-specific preference.
reasoning.deletionTest: Structural evaluation and opioid history protect primary-pattern attribution. Body timing and distribution distinguish the procedures. Removing the table removes the subtype-specific reason to favor the key.
reasoning.cueAttack: The task supplies neither a diagnosis nor a desired myotomy length. All three options are actual definitive procedures. The key's tailored phrase describes the operation and remains a weak potential cue requiring independent review. No categorical failure of Heller is taught.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three initial definitive procedures with comparable care phase and named techniques.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The credible error is selecting a familiar Heller or balloon plan without applying the body pattern. Expert-opinion ranking makes exact clinician review important.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: First chart-review node. Feedback covers the initial subtype and procedure, and omits the later test-selection rule.
reasoning.remainingRisk: Melissa must confirm POEM over the offered Heller option for this exact extent. ACG accepts tailored Heller and SAGES preference is expert opinion.

nodes.identityReason: The assigned bank lacks a scored assessment of recurrent symptoms after myotomy using objective bolus clearance.
nodes.objective: Choose objective clearance assessment when recurrent symptoms and post-myotomy pressure findings disagree.
nodes.task: Which investigation should next assess {patientName}'s recurrent symptoms after POEM?
nodes.currentUpdate: The later record documents POEM followed by a period of comfortable eating. Food now pauses and fluid returns at night. Repeat manometry shows junction relaxation within the laboratory interval and no residual premature contractions. Her weight and oral hydration are maintained.

choices.label: Repeat positional high-resolution esophageal manometry
choices.rationale: The adequate repeat pressure study has answered the residual spasm and relaxation questions. Another pressure study will not directly establish the degree of retained bolus.
choices.temptation: Use a normal relaxation value as the sole treatment-success measure or repeat it when symptoms disagree.
choices.correctUnder: The prior pressure acquisition is technically inadequate or a new question about residual spasm or relaxation remains.

choices.label: Upright timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
choices.rationale: The current uncertainty is actual clearance despite improved relaxation measurements. Timed barium testing is the guideline-supported first objective assessment of recurrent post-treatment symptoms.
choices.temptation: The key depends on recognizing that pressure relaxation and bolus clearance are different observations.
choices.correctUnder: Persistent or recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia therapy require objective emptying assessment.

choices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
choices.rationale: Reflux is a real alternative after POEM. Clearance assessment should first characterize the food-and-fluid hold-up in this recurrent swallowing presentation, with reflux evaluation as indicated by the resulting assessment.
choices.temptation: Attribute nocturnal fluid return directly to reflux after POEM.
choices.correctUnder: Clearance has been adequately assessed and the unresolved question is whether symptoms correlate with pathologic reflux.

nodes.explanation: A lower junction relaxation pressure does not establish emptying. Assess the recurrent symptoms with timed barium clearance and integrate the result with the rest of the foregut evaluation. This result is still pending at this point in the chart review.

reasoning.interpret: Identify the discordance between recurrent retention-like symptoms and improved pressure findings.
reasoning.apply: Choose a direct clearance assessment instead of equating normalized relaxation with treatment success.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Food pauses with nocturnal return despite an adequate manometry showing improved junction relaxation.
reasoning.counterfactual: If adequate emptying is already documented and the remaining complaint is burning with uncertain reflux correlation, pH-impedance becomes the relevant offered study.
reasoning.deletionTest: Prior response establishes recurrence. Normal relaxation prevents automatic repetition of a diagnostic test. The current symptom pattern establishes the clearance question. Deleting the update leaves no reason for post-treatment testing.
reasoning.cueAttack: Three specific studies each receive a timing proposal. No task word repeats barium or emptying. The key is not uniquely cautious or uniquely estimated. Reflux remains credible after POEM.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three investigations at the same reassessment stage, each with acquisition-specific identity and wait metadata.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The resident must resist both normal-IRP reassurance and immediate reflux attribution after an effective initial myotomy.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Earlier feedback identifies a subtype-specific initial procedure and never states the post-treatment test rule. The later clearance and mucosal results are not visible yet.
reasoning.remainingRisk: The contrast-swallow profile is an existing placeholder. Manager must preserve the full timed-series scope when registering its estimate.

nodes.identityReason: This consequence-of-myotomy construct distinguishes objective inflammation with adequate clearance from recurrent junction obstruction. Coordinate its boundary with the GERD worker.
nodes.objective: Use clearance and mucosal findings to choose treatment for symptoms mistakenly attributed to recurrent outflow obstruction.
nodes.task: Which treatment should now address {patientName}'s post-POEM symptoms?
nodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Endoscopy shows distal erosive esophagitis, with no retained food or fixed narrowing. She reports burning and sour fluid return and is taking no acid-suppressive medicine.

choices.label: Arrange pneumatic dilation of the junction
choices.rationale: Symptoms after POEM can reflect residual outflow resistance, but the acquired clearance and endoscopic findings favor mucosal reflux injury in this record.
choices.temptation: Treat every recurrent post-myotomy symptom by further disrupting the junction.
choices.correctUnder: Objective reassessment demonstrates recurrent junction obstruction and the patient is suitable for dilation and rescue.

choices.label: Start oral omeprazole and reassess symptoms
choices.rationale: Objectively documented erosive injury with effective clearance supports acid suppression before another junction procedure.
choices.temptation: The key requires reconciling the normal passage findings with the abnormal mucosa rather than relying on the symptom label.
choices.correctUnder: Post-myotomy reflux injury is documented and there is no acquired evidence of recurrent obstructive retention.

choices.label: Arrange repeat peroral endoscopic myotomy
choices.rationale: A repeat myotomy may address an incomplete prior myotomy. The present studies do not show that target, while esophagitis supplies a treatable competing cause.
choices.temptation: Anchor on the original motor diagnosis despite a new objective cause for the symptoms.
choices.correctUnder: Comprehensive reassessment identifies persistent obstructive physiology from an inadequate myotomy and a foregut team selects redo POEM.

nodes.explanation: The acquired clearance and endoscopic findings redirect treatment toward reflux injury. Oral omeprazole is the appropriate offered initial treatment. Further junction disruption requires a persisting obstructive target, which this reassessment has not demonstrated.

reasoning.interpret: Combine effective passage with erosive mucosal injury to distinguish a post-treatment complication from recurrent outflow obstruction.
reasoning.apply: Select acid suppression instead of another junction-disrupting procedure.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Prompt liquid and tablet passage coexist with distal erosive esophagitis.
reasoning.counterfactual: Persistent retention and tablet hold-up at a poorly opening junction with no erosive lesion would redirect assessment toward an obstructive target and could support dilation after specialist review.
reasoning.deletionTest: Clearance distinguishes the motor-treatment target. Endoscopy identifies the new cause. Current medication status establishes an initial treatment opportunity. Without these acquired findings the prior node still calls for evaluation.
reasoning.cueAttack: The task says post-POEM symptoms and never calls them reflux. Each option is a named current treatment. The PPI is the only medicine because the clinically credible errors are repeat procedures. That category difference is a residual review concern rather than a claimed cue-free guarantee.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three present treatments for recurrent post-myotomy symptoms. All investigations are already completed.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The intended difficulty is changing a motor-treatment plan when objective clearance and a new mucosal finding disagree with the original diagnosis.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Prior feedback gives no PPI answer and no esophagitis result. The new endoscopy changes the action. The learner cannot infer this key from the previous pressure record alone.
reasoning.remainingRisk: GERD ownership overlaps the consequence-of-myotomy scope. Manager must coordinate placement. Melissa must confirm exact PPI and repeat-intervention ranking.

reviewedItems.name: Ruth Ellis
reviewedItems.presentation: {patientName}, an 81-year-old woman, attends clinic because food and drinks pause behind the sternum and increasingly limit her meals.

nodes.identityReason: No assigned variant tests why an apparently less invasive pneumatic dilation can remain unsuitable when perforation rescue is prohibitive.
nodes.objective: Integrate documented outflow physiology and procedural rescue risk when selecting initial symptom relief.
nodes.task: Which initial procedure best fits {patientName}'s swallowing findings and perioperative assessment?
nodes.currentUpdate: Endoscopy and cardia imaging show no structural lesion. Adequate manometry shows failed body contractions with impaired junction relaxation, and the timed contrast study retains liquid above the junction. She has oxygen-dependent lung disease. The anesthesia record considers a brief sedated endoscopy acceptable but describes prolonged general anesthesia and a major rescue operation as prohibitive.

choices.label: Endoscopic pneumatic dilation of the junction
choices.rationale: Dilation can provide durable relief in suitable patients, but its perforation risk requires a viable rescue plan. The anesthetic assessment is consequential even though the primary treatment is endoscopic.
choices.temptation: Equate an endoscopic intervention with freedom from major rescue risk.
choices.correctUnder: The patient is suitable for dilation and could undergo rescue repair if perforation occurs.

choices.label: Endoscopic botulinum toxin injection at the sphincter
choices.rationale: This is a guideline-supported symptom-relief option when definitive treatments are unsuitable. Its usually temporary benefit must be weighed against the documented procedural and rescue risks.
choices.temptation: The key requires considering the consequence of a complication, not just the planned route of the procedure.
choices.correctUnder: Established achalasia causes symptoms in a patient unsuitable for definitive junction therapies.

choices.label: Endoscopic peroral myotomy of the distal junction
choices.rationale: POEM is a definitive treatment with a greater anesthetic and complication-management burden than the limited sedated intervention described here.
choices.temptation: Select a durable endoscopic therapy while treating the anesthesia findings as relevant only to laparoscopy.
choices.correctUnder: A fully assessed patient can tolerate definitive myotomy and its complication management.

nodes.explanation: The motor and clearance findings support a junction-relaxation disorder, but treatment selection also depends on anesthesia and rescue risk. Botulinum toxin is the appropriate offered initial symptom-relief option for this risk profile. Age alone does not determine that choice.

reasoning.interpret: Recognize established symptomatic outflow physiology after structural evaluation.
reasoning.apply: Assess the full procedural and rescue burden before selecting an endoscopic treatment.
reasoning.decidingObservation: A brief sedated procedure is acceptable but major perforation rescue and prolonged anesthesia are prohibitive.
reasoning.counterfactual: If the same physiology occurs in someone who can tolerate definitive therapy and perforation rescue and who chooses a dilation strategy, pneumatic dilation becomes a reasonable offered option over temporary injection.
reasoning.deletionTest: The acquired motor and retention findings establish the target. The anesthesia assessment separates three otherwise relevant endoscopic procedures. Age is patient context and is not a cutoff.
reasoning.cueAttack: Every label is an endoscopic intervention with comparable specificity. The clinical risk assessment is necessary and is given once. Removed an explicit author-written declaration that she is ineligible for definitive therapy. No exact comorbidity cutoff is invented.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three initial junction-directed procedures. The comparison is not diagnostic workup versus treatment.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The closest error is recommending pneumatic dilation because it avoids the planned laparoscopic operation while overlooking its rescue requirement.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Standalone. Temporary benefit is explained after the choice and supplies no later key.
reasoning.remainingRisk: Melissa must confirm the exact anesthesia-risk presentation and procedure comparison. The assessment is a constructed individual clinical record.

reviewedItems.name: Owen Clark
reviewedItems.presentation: {patientName}, a 58-year-old man, attends clinic with intermittent food-and-liquid hold-up after endoscopy and mucosal sampling found no explanatory lesion.

nodes.identityReason: Existing EGJOO appears as a diagnostic foil. This new construct scores the additional evidence needed to establish its clinical relevance.
nodes.objective: Distinguish a retained-peristalsis pressure pattern from conclusive achalasia and choose a complementary obstruction assessment.
nodes.task: Which additional investigation should inform {patientName}'s junction-treatment assessment?
nodes.currentUpdate: An adequate junction-crossing study has elevated median relaxation pressure in both positions. Propagated contractions follow most swallows, and intrabolus pressure is raised in most supine swallows. The symptom episodes occur during the study. He takes no opioids and has no prior foregut operation.

choices.label: Repeat the routine positional water-swallow manometry study
choices.rationale: The existing acquisition is adequate. Repeating the same pressure protocol does not add the independent emptying evidence needed to establish the observed pattern's clinical relevance.
choices.temptation: Treat a second similar manometry result as independent corroboration of clinically important obstruction.
choices.correctUnder: The original pressure acquisition has a technical limitation or an unreconciled position/protocol problem.

choices.label: Obtain ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
choices.rationale: Reflux monitoring can address a reflux hypothesis, but it does not establish whether the current preserved-peristalsis outflow pattern impedes passage.
choices.temptation: Attribute regurgitation-like hold-up to reflux because some body contractions persist.
choices.correctUnder: Obstructive physiology has been adequately assessed and the unresolved question concerns reflux burden or symptom association.

choices.label: Obtain upright timed barium esophagography with a tablet
choices.rationale: The retained peristalsis distinguishes this pattern from conclusive achalasia. A complementary passage study can establish clinically relevant obstruction before choosing junction therapy.
choices.temptation: The key requires interpreting retained peristalsis and then seeking independent functional corroboration.
choices.correctUnder: A symptomatic manometric EGJOO pattern remains to be corroborated by an accepted supportive study.

nodes.explanation: Elevated relaxation pressure with retained peristalsis does not establish conclusive achalasia. Use a complementary study to assess the clinical relevance of the outflow pattern. Timed barium with tablet passage is the appropriate offered study. FLIP is another accepted supportive approach.

reasoning.interpret: Recognize retained peristalsis despite positional relaxation-pressure and intrabolus abnormalities.
reasoning.apply: Seek an accepted independent obstruction assessment before treating the manometric category as a clinical diagnosis.
reasoning.decidingObservation: The study is adequate and demonstrates preserved propagated contractions, so more of the same pressure protocol is not the missing evidence.
reasoning.counterfactual: If the catheter never crossed the junction or the primary-position series was unusable, repeating an adequate pressure study would become the relevant offered next step.
reasoning.deletionTest: Structural and exposure history constrain secondary explanations. Peristalsis distinguishes the category. Adequacy separates complementary testing from repetition. Removing those observations makes the key unsupported.
reasoning.cueAttack: The task names no barium, emptying endpoint or gold-standard property. All three options are investigations with matched wait metadata. The available FLIP alternative is discussed only in feedback to avoid two defensible supportive-study choices.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three additional investigations before a junction-treatment decision.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The resident must separate a manometric category from a clinically conclusive obstructive disorder instead of immediately applying the achalasia treatment pathway.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Standalone. No prior answer supplies the EGJOO or corroboration rule.
reasoning.remainingRisk: The constructed phrase several supine swallows is qualitative. Melissa must confirm sufficient protocol detail and the exact test ranking.

reviewedItems.name: Leah Foster
reviewedItems.presentation: {patientName}, a 63-year-old woman, attends clinic with continuing food-and-liquid dysphagia and regurgitation after structural evaluation found no junction lesion.

nodes.identityReason: The live acquisition questions favor assisted completion. This new boundary asks what to do after assistance has also failed to produce usable measurements.
nodes.objective: Choose complementary distensibility assessment after genuine repeated inability to complete pressure testing.
nodes.task: Which investigation should now advance {patientName}'s motor-disorder assessment?
nodes.currentUpdate: The initial catheter study stopped during retching. During a later endoscopically assisted attempt, the catheter crossed the junction, but after recovery she repeatedly displaced it and the separated-swallow series remained unusable. The recent timed contrast study showed substantial retention above a smooth distal taper.

choices.label: Repeat endoscopically assisted high-resolution manometry
choices.rationale: Assisted completion is appropriate after an initial placement failure. It has now also failed to yield usable post-recovery measurements, making a complementary method reasonable.
choices.temptation: Apply the usual failed-catheter repair repeatedly without considering the documented assisted failure.
choices.correctUnder: The initial failure was a placement problem and a feasible assisted attempt has not yet been completed.

choices.label: Obtain endoscopic FLIP topography and junction distensibility
choices.rationale: Persistent incomplete manometry despite assisted placement is an accepted setting for FLIP assessment. It can add motor/outflow information beyond the already acquired retention study.
choices.temptation: The key requires distinguishing failure to acquire pressure data from the supportive obstruction observations already available.
choices.correctUnder: Obstructive symptoms persist and standard pressure testing remains incomplete despite assisted placement.

choices.label: Repeat timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
choices.rationale: A contrast study has already demonstrated retention. Repeating that same observation will not supply the complementary physiology sought after repeated pressure-acquisition failure.
choices.temptation: Retreat to a familiar supportive study that is already informative but does not answer the remaining question.
choices.correctUnder: The prior contrast acquisition was inadequate or the clinical question now concerns a changed clearance trajectory.

nodes.explanation: The record contains a real failure after assisted placement and an already informative retention study. FLIP is a supported complementary route in that circumstance. It does not recreate a complete manometric subtype or prove that an irreversible procedure is indicated.

reasoning.interpret: Determine that the pressure assessment remains unusable despite an actual assisted attempt, while retention has already been acquired.
reasoning.apply: Select a supported complementary method rather than repeat an unsuccessful acquisition strategy or the same emptying observation.
reasoning.decidingObservation: The post-recovery series was unusable after assisted crossing, rather than merely absent from an exported report.
reasoning.counterfactual: If the only failure was blind placement and there had been no assisted attempt, assisted HRM would be the appropriate offered way to obtain a complete pressure classification.
reasoning.deletionTest: The two acquisition episodes establish the important boundary. The existing contrast result prevents a generic barium choice. Removing assisted failure restores the live bank's familiar completion pathway.
reasoning.cueAttack: Three genuine diagnostic paths have estimates. The task names no distensibility goal. The failed-assistance record is decision-critical chronology, rather than a sentence announcing an unattempted key.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three investigations after incomplete pressure testing. No treatment competes with diagnostic completion.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The closest error is repeating the familiar assisted-HRM rule even after that method has failed to yield interpretable acquisition.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Standalone. This variant must not directly follow the frozen assisted-HRM task as another score of the same unresolved acquisition.
reasoning.remainingRisk: The generic upper-endoscopy timing profile is a placeholder for FLIP. A new service is not executed. Manager must register the exact planned-test identity.

reviewedItems.name: Gavin Moore
reviewedItems.presentation: {patientName}, a 60-year-old man, attends clinic with persistent food-and-liquid dysphagia after endoscopy and junction imaging showed no structural explanation.

nodes.identityReason: Assigned recognition variants use clearly elevated relaxation pressures. This new decision concerns unresolved outflow obstruction when the measured pressure is at the upper normal boundary.
nodes.objective: Avoid closing the achalasia assessment from an upper-normal relaxation value when all body contractions fail.
nodes.task: Which investigation should next clarify {patientName}'s swallowing disorder?
nodes.currentUpdate: An adequate positional pressure study records failed contractions after every separated swallow. Median junction-relaxation values sit at this laboratory's upper normal limit in both positions. No normal propagation appears during alternate-position swallows. He takes no opioids.

choices.label: Extend manometry with a standardized solid-meal recording
choices.rationale: A meal challenge is useful when an adequate liquid study leaves episodic food symptoms unexplained. This study already demonstrates universal body failure with unresolved junction opening, warranting complementary assessment.
choices.temptation: Treat dysphagia with a formally normal relaxation number as a symptom-provocation problem.
choices.correctUnder: Routine liquid acquisition is adequate and unrevealing while meal-associated symptoms remain unexplained.

choices.label: Obtain upright timed barium esophagography with a tablet
choices.rationale: The failed body series with upper-limit relaxation values remains inconclusive for achalasia versus absent contractility. A supportive passage study can clarify the obstruction question.
choices.temptation: The key requires recognizing uncertainty within the reference boundary rather than treating normal-range as complete exclusion.
choices.correctUnder: Dysphagia and an inconclusive achalasia/absent-contractility pattern require supportive assessment.

choices.label: Obtain ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
choices.rationale: A reflex reflux workup would leave the unresolved emptying and junction-opening question unanswered in this presentation.
choices.temptation: Assign a reflux-associated hypomotility explanation as soon as the relaxation number is printed inside the reference interval.
choices.correctUnder: The obstruction question has been resolved and a reflux mechanism is the remaining specific diagnostic concern.

nodes.explanation: Universal body failure with relaxation values at the upper normal boundary can remain inconclusive. Obtain supportive obstruction assessment instead of assigning a final label from the reference flag. Timed barium is appropriate among the offered studies. FLIP is another supported complementary option.

reasoning.interpret: Recognize that all failed contractions plus an upper-limit relaxation value do not settle achalasia versus absent contractility.
reasoning.apply: Select complementary passage assessment before allowing the printed normal flag to close the workup.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Body failure is universal in an adequate study and relaxation is at the boundary in both positions.
reasoning.counterfactual: If separated liquid swallows have normal propagation and relaxation but fail to reproduce solid-food episodes, a standardized-meal extension becomes the relevant offered next study.
reasoning.deletionTest: The location within the normal interval matters. Universal failure distinguishes this from an unrevealing liquid series. Removing either observation changes the differential and next-study ranking.
reasoning.cueAttack: All choices are specific investigations with estimates. The task has no normal-pressure exclusion language. FLIP is kept outside the answer set because it is another defensible supportive test.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three additional investigations after a completed baseline physiology study.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The credible error is treating a reference-interval flag as a sufficient exclusion and choosing another symptom-protocol or reflux pathway.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Standalone. This shares the barium test with the EGJOO item but the discriminator is upper-normal IRP with absent peristalsis rather than retained peristalsis with elevated pressure.
reasoning.remainingRisk: Clinician review must confirm that the constructed upper-limit record supplies adequate uncertainty without a fabricated device-specific cutoff.

reviewedItems.name: Elena Ward
reviewedItems.presentation: {patientName}, a 54-year-old woman, attends clinic after discharge for aspiration-related respiratory illness. The founder reviews her earlier and current outside foregut records with her.

nodes.identityReason: No assigned item tests organ-preserving salvage after endoscopic treatment failure with evidence of an incomplete myotomy.
nodes.objective: Use residual junction obstruction and favorable anatomy to consider Heller salvage before esophagectomy.
nodes.task: Which plan best fits {patientName}'s earlier referral after dilation and POEM had failed?
nodes.currentUpdate: At that earlier referral she was fit for major surgery but continued to retain food after graded dilation and POEM. The timed study showed a relatively straight esophagus with hold-up at the junction. Endoscopy showed no reflux stricture or malignancy. Distensibility remained reduced, and review of the POEM report documented that the muscle division had stopped short of the gastric extension.

choices.label: Refer for esophagectomy with reconstruction assessment
choices.rationale: Resection can be appropriate after exhausted treatment in severely distorted disease. Favorable anatomy and a documented incomplete myotomy leave an organ-preserving target at this earlier stage.
choices.temptation: Count two failed treatment families as automatic exhaustion of salvage.
choices.correctUnder: Severe distorted anatomy and disabling retention persist after adequate therapies, with no useful residual junction target.

choices.label: Refer for Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication
choices.rationale: The record identifies an incomplete prior myotomy and anatomy conducive to salvage. Guidance supports considering Heller before resection in this setting.
choices.temptation: The key depends on distinguishing a failed intervention from a fully treated but irreversibly dysfunctional reservoir.
choices.correctUnder: A fit patient has favorable anatomy and residual obstruction from incomplete myotomy after failed dilation and POEM.

choices.label: Refer for sphincter botulinum toxin injection
choices.rationale: Temporary symptom relief is appropriate when definitive therapy is unsuitable. Her fitness and residual correctable target support considering definitive salvage here.
choices.temptation: Avoid a major salvage decision by defaulting to the lower-burden palliative procedure.
choices.correctUnder: The patient cannot undergo appropriate definitive treatment and symptom relief is the agreed objective.

nodes.explanation: Treatment failure does not by itself establish an exhausted organ. Favorable anatomy and documented incomplete myotomy support considering Heller salvage before resection. The exact salvage plan requires a specialized foregut assessment.

reasoning.interpret: Identify a persistent correctable junction target instead of inferring irreversible end-stage failure from treatment count.
reasoning.apply: Choose organ-preserving salvage assessment before esophagectomy in favorable anatomy.
reasoning.decidingObservation: The esophagus is relatively straight and the prior division did not reach the gastric extension.
reasoning.counterfactual: Severe sigmoid distortion with a patent, adequately myotomized junction and continuing disabling retention after completed therapies would shift the offered referral toward esophagectomy assessment.
reasoning.deletionTest: Prior treatments establish salvage phase. Fitness distinguishes definitive from temporary therapy. Anatomy and incomplete myotomy supply the organ-preserving target. Deleting those findings leaves the treatment-count shortcut unresolved.
reasoning.cueAttack: All three options are referrals for named treatments. The key has no uniquely cautious assessment qualifier. The actual operative record is necessary evidence rather than an author-written correctable-lesion label.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three treatment referrals for an already characterized failed-treatment state.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The resident must prioritize mechanism and anatomy over the number of prior failures while avoiding premature resection.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: Earlier historical stage. The patient's current age and clinic context remain in the header. Feedback does not specify the later anatomy or a future esophagectomy answer.
reasoning.remainingRisk: Evidence for exact salvage sequencing is low certainty. Redo POEM is also plausible in some patients and is not ranked against Heller in this option set.

nodes.identityReason: This distinct later construct scores the boundary where severe reservoir failure persists despite a completed myotomy and further junction treatment lacks a demonstrated target.
nodes.objective: Recognize severe anatomic reservoir failure after adequate junction therapies and select a high-volume esophageal-center referral.
nodes.task: Which referral best fits {patientName}'s current outside-hospital findings?
nodes.currentUpdate: The later records document completion of Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication and initial improvement. At her current admission she again regurgitated retained food and developed aspiration-related illness. After respiratory recovery, the esophagram showed a markedly dilated sigmoid esophagus with dependent pools persisting through the timed series. Endoscopy and FLIP showed a widely opening junction with no fixed stricture. The operative record confirms a completed myotomy. Nutrition and cardiopulmonary assessment support considering major surgery after optimization.

choices.label: Refer for repeat POEM across the distal junction
choices.rationale: Further muscle division can treat an incomplete myotomy. The current record instead shows adequate junction opening and severe distorted-reservoir retention after completed therapies.
choices.temptation: Assume a recurrent symptom always indicates recurrent sphincter resistance.
choices.correctUnder: Reassessment identifies an incomplete myotomy and an anatomic target suited to another junction procedure.

choices.label: Refer to a high-volume center for esophagectomy assessment
choices.rationale: Disabling retention, aspiration consequences, severe distortion and failure despite adequate junction treatment support specialized resection assessment. The referral does not predetermine the final operation.
choices.temptation: The key requires recognizing a changed mechanism after earlier organ-preserving salvage was appropriate.
choices.correctUnder: A potentially fit patient has severe distorted anatomy and consequential retention after adequate prior therapies.

choices.label: Refer for further pneumatic dilation of the junction
choices.rationale: Dilation can help recurrent junction resistance, but the current studies show a widely opening junction and a severely distorted retaining reservoir.
choices.temptation: Choose another lower-burden junction treatment despite the absence of its demonstrated target.
choices.correctUnder: A fit patient has recurrent obstructive resistance at the junction and a foregut team selects dilation with rescue planning.

nodes.explanation: The later findings change the problem from incomplete junction treatment to severe distorted-reservoir failure. A high-volume esophageal center should assess resection after nutritional and cardiopulmonary optimization. Diameter alone and the count of earlier interventions do not decide this referral.

reasoning.interpret: Distinguish persistent dependent retention in a severely distorted reservoir from residual obstruction at an incompletely treated junction.
reasoning.apply: Select specialist esophagectomy assessment after adequate prior treatments and recovery sufficient to consider major surgery.
reasoning.decidingObservation: The junction opens widely after a completed myotomy while substantial dependent retention and aspiration consequences persist.
reasoning.counterfactual: A relatively straight esophagus with retained material above a poorly opening junction and documented incomplete division would restore an organ-preserving junction-salvage referral such as redo myotomy.
reasoning.deletionTest: Completed treatment and actual opening establish the absence of the previous target. Distortion and retention identify reservoir failure. Aspiration establishes consequence. Recovery and fitness support considering major surgery. Removing the new update leaves the earlier salvage plan appropriate.
reasoning.cueAttack: All labels are referrals for specific procedures, and all include a named target. No invented diameter threshold or end-stage diagnosis appears before choice. The key's high-volume wording is clinically necessary but is a possible specificity cue for independent review.
reasoning.stageAudit: Three referral destinations after a completed current anatomic and physiologic reassessment.
reasoning.difficultyReason: The resident must change direction from the previous organ-preserving answer when the current mechanism differs, while respecting the morbidity of resection.
reasoning.sequenceAudit: The prior explanation gives the earlier salvage rationale and does not name the later referral. Current widely opening junction and distorted retention are new. Delete them and the previous answer would remain appropriate.
reasoning.remainingRisk: Low-certainty individualized surgery. Melissa must confirm that the constructed observations support resection assessment and that current recovery is adequately represented. No acute hospital care is executed in clinic.

concepts.learningObjective: Use actual symptom and pressure changes after coordinated opioid adjustment when deciding whether to retain an achalasia myotomy plan.
Integrate a spastic achalasia pattern and its body extent when selecting an initial definitive procedure.
Choose objective clearance assessment when recurrent symptoms and post-myotomy pressure findings disagree.
Use clearance and mucosal findings to choose treatment for symptoms mistakenly attributed to recurrent outflow obstruction.
Integrate documented outflow physiology and procedural rescue risk when selecting initial symptom relief.
Distinguish a retained-peristalsis pressure pattern from conclusive achalasia and choose a complementary obstruction assessment.
Choose complementary distensibility assessment after genuine repeated inability to complete pressure testing.
Avoid closing the achalasia assessment from an upper-normal relaxation value when all body contractions fail.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Her initial record documents progressive food-and-liquid dysphagia with swallowing-related pain. Endoscopy and cross-sectional assessment show no junction lesion. She uses no opioids and the anesthesia evaluation permits either endoscopic or laparoscopic myotomy.
decisionNodes.stem: Which initial procedure is best supported by {patientName}'s evaluation?

answerChoices.label: Laparoscopic Heller myotomy with Dor fundoplication
answerChoices.rationale: Surgical myotomy remains a legitimate option. The substantial spastic body component supports a tailored approach and the current SAGES panel favors POEM in this subtype.

answerChoices.label: Graded pneumatic dilation of the distal junction
answerChoices.rationale: Dilation is a definitive option in selected achalasia patients, but treating junction resistance with a balloon does not address the demonstrated spastic body extent as a tailored myotomy can.

answerChoices.label: Tailored peroral endoscopic myotomy
answerChoices.rationale: The adequate study has impaired relaxation and premature/failed responses without normal peristalsis. A tailored POEM can include the involved body segment and follows the current SAGES preference for type III.

decisionNodes.explanation: Impaired relaxation with premature or failed swallows and absent normal peristalsis supports a spastic achalasia pattern. decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The later record documents POEM followed by a period of comfortable eating. Food now pauses and fluid returns at night. answerChoices.label: Repeat positional high-resolution esophageal manometry
answerChoices.rationale: The adequate repeat pressure study has answered the residual spasm and relaxation questions. Another pressure study will not directly establish the degree of retained bolus.

answerChoices.label: Upright timed barium esophagography with tablet passage
answerChoices.rationale: The current uncertainty is actual clearance despite improved relaxation measurements. Timed barium testing is the guideline-supported first objective assessment of recurrent post-treatment symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Ambulatory esophageal pH-impedance reflux monitoring
answerChoices.rationale: Reflux is a real alternative after POEM. Clearance assessment should first characterize the food-and-fluid hold-up in this recurrent swallowing presentation, with reflux evaluation as indicated by the resulting assessment.

decisionNodes.explanation: A lower junction relaxation pressure does not establish emptying. Assess the recurrent symptoms with timed barium clearance and integrate the result with the rest of the foregut evaluation. This result is still pending at this point in the chart review.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. answerChoices.rationale: Objectively documented erosive injury with effective clearance supports acid suppression before another junction procedure.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At that earlier referral she was fit for major surgery but continued to retain food after graded dilation and POEM. The timed study showed a relatively straight esophagus with hold-up at the junction. Endoscopy showed no reflux stricture or malignancy. Distensibility remained reduced, and review of the POEM report documented that the muscle division had stopped short of the gastric extension.
decisionNodes.stem: Which plan best fits {patientName}'s earlier referral after dilation and POEM had failed?

answerChoices.label: Refer for esophagectomy with reconstruction assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Resection can be appropriate after exhausted treatment in severely distorted disease. Favorable anatomy and a documented incomplete myotomy leave an organ-preserving target at this earlier stage.

answerChoices.label: Refer for Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication
answerChoices.rationale: The record identifies an incomplete prior myotomy and anatomy conducive to salvage. Guidance supports considering Heller before resection in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Refer for sphincter botulinum toxin injection
answerChoices.rationale: Temporary symptom relief is appropriate when definitive therapy is unsuitable. Her fitness and residual correctable target support considering definitive salvage here.

decisionNodes.explanation: Treatment failure does not by itself establish an exhausted organ. Favorable anatomy and documented incomplete myotomy support considering Heller salvage before resection. The exact salvage plan requires a specialized foregut assessment.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The later records document completion of Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication and initial improvement. At her current admission she again regurgitated retained food and developed aspiration-related illness. After respiratory recovery, the esophagram showed a markedly dilated sigmoid esophagus with dependent pools persisting through the timed series. Endoscopy and FLIP showed a widely opening junction with no fixed stricture. The operative record confirms a completed myotomy. Nutrition and cardiopulmonary assessment support considering major surgery after optimization.
decisionNodes.stem: Which referral best fits {patientName}'s current outside-hospital findings?

answerChoices.label: Refer for repeat POEM across the distal junction
answerChoices.rationale: Further muscle division can treat an incomplete myotomy. The current record instead shows adequate junction opening and severe distorted-reservoir retention after completed therapies.

answerChoices.label: Refer to a high-volume center for esophagectomy assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Disabling retention, aspiration consequences, severe distortion and failure despite adequate junction treatment support specialized resection assessment. The referral does not predetermine the final operation.

answerChoices.label: Refer for further pneumatic dilation of the junction
answerChoices.rationale: Dilation can help recurrent junction resistance, but the current studies show a widely opening junction and a severely distorted retaining reservoir.

decisionNodes.explanation: The later findings change the problem from incomplete junction treatment to severe distorted-reservoir failure. A high-volume esophageal center should assess resection after nutritional and cardiopulmonary optimization. Diameter alone and the count of earlier interventions do not decide this referral.

record.title: Achalasia treatment when operative rescue is prohibitive

cues.phrase: a brief sedated endoscopy acceptable but describes prolonged general anesthesia and a major rescue operation as prohibitive
cues.why: The assessment strongly directs risk-based selection, but it is a necessary constraint rather than a gratuitous permission sentence. All labels are endoscopic. Choosing injection over dilation still requires knowing the latter's perforation/rescue implications; a wording-only match does not settle that close comparison.

fairness: The failed contractions, impaired relaxation and retained contrast support the motor/outflow disorder. The resident must then apply both anesthesia and rescue constraints: an endoscopic approach is not automatically suitable merely because it avoids a planned operation.

Botulinum toxin is the defensible best offered initial procedure for the represented risk assessment. Pneumatic dilation is the meaningful near-miss because the patient cannot tolerate major rescue if perforation occurs. The myotomy alternative requires a different anesthesia burden. Age alone is not the discriminator.

The named patient, age, sex, symptoms and complete task agree. This standalone node has no missing predecessor. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the constructed perioperative assessment still requires exact clinical sign-off.

This is high-yield treatment-selection reasoning. The combination of a motor diagnosis and procedure-specific rescue risk earns two consequential steps, although the explicit anesthesia assessment keeps it moderate rather than hard.
suggestions: Preserve the decision-critical rescue restriction. Do not remove it in an effort to make the item harder or replace it with age-based eligibility.

For future feedback refinement, explicitly explain why dilation remains a poor choice despite being endoscopic: its perforation risk can require rescue the patient cannot tolerate. Any wording change would be a new exact version requiring review.

record.title: Preserved propagation with elevated junction pressure
fairness: The resident must interpret preserved propagation alongside elevated positional relaxation and intrabolus pressures, then recognize that symptom reproduction during manometry does not itself establish clinically relevant obstruction. Timed barium with a tablet is the best offered complementary assessment.

Solid-meal manometry is a real competing physiologic investigation, not simply a repeat of the completed liquid-swallow series. The adequate symptom-reproducing pressure study makes independent passage assessment more informative for the present unresolved issue. Meal provocation can provide supportive information; the explanation should not be read as claiming it is never useful in this pattern.

The absence of an explanatory endoscopic lesion, opioid use and prior foregut surgery addresses important confounders without supplying the diagnosis. No invented numerical cutoff is needed to solve this represented pattern. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.

The standalone presentation and task are complete. Distinguishing an outflow-obstruction pattern from conclusive achalasia and selecting confirmatory testing is relevant general-surgery motility content; this high-yield judgment is qualitative, not a verified exam-frequency claim.
The options use comparable investigation labels. No unique phrase match, diagnosis label, teaching sentence, absolute or common-component pattern selects the key without clinical knowledge.
suggestions: Retain the distinction between supportive symptom/pressure observations and complementary evidence of obstruction.
Keep the meal-provocation explanation qualified: its lower priority here does not make it generally useless in evaluating outflow-obstruction patterns.

record.title: Physiologic assessment after unusable assisted manometry

cues.phrase: no mass or focal wall abnormality / Endoscopic ultrasound of the cardia and junction wall
cues.why: The negative wall finding lexically weakens the wall-imaging option. This is a residual elimination cue, but structural observations and the gradual stable-weight course are needed to rank further structural evaluation fairly. They do not exclude occult infiltration with certainty, and the final choice still requires understanding which physiologic assessment is feasible after failed manometry.

fairness: The acquisition history makes clear that crossing the junction was achieved but did not yield usable swallow recordings. The resident must avoid treating attempted placement as a completed physiologic test, then select FLIP to assess junction opening and motor response in the setting of demonstrated retention.

FLIP is the best offered next test. EUS remains plausible when occult secondary obstruction is suspected, but the gradual course, stable weight and described structural assessment lower that priority here. They do not prove that every infiltrative process has been excluded. Reflux monitoring does not resolve the demonstrated retention and missing motor assessment.

The explanation appropriately limits FLIP: it does not supply a complete pressure-based subtype or independently authorize irreversible treatment. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Exact test-priority verification was not performed because network and source review are outside this task.

The standalone node gives sufficient chronology and a complete task. No prior answer is needed. The present diagnostic competitors are different investigations, and the key is not merely the only untried test.

This is a useful advanced niche within a high-yield disease area. The precise FLIP-after-failed-assisted-manometry decision is narrower than commonly tested achalasia diagnosis and treatment; unfamiliarity with FLIP should not be mistaken for hard reasoning.
suggestions: Retain as optional advanced coverage rather than use it to satisfy core high-yield or hard-item targets.
Preserve the distinction between lower suspicion for a wall lesion and exclusion of secondary disease. Keep the failed acquisition observations and FLIP limitations explicit.

answerChoices.rationale: Endoscopy can identify reflux injury or a post-treatment narrowing and may be complementary in the full reassessment. answerChoices.rationale: Normal measured relaxation and absence of residual spasm do not establish bolus emptying. Upright timed barium testing directly assesses clearance and is the ACG first-line objective investigation for recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia treatment.

answerChoices.rationale: Nocturnal fluid return after POEM makes reflux a credible mechanism. Her recurrent food hold-up still requires objective clearance assessment first; reflux monitoring answers a different question once clearance and structural findings have been considered.

decisionNodes.stem: Which medication plan should next address {patientName}'s persistent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent upright timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Endoscopy shows distal mucosal breaks, without retained food or a fixed narrowing. She describes burning and sour fluid return, especially after lying down. Bottle review confirms conventional delayed-release omeprazole taken every day at bedtime, several hours after dinner.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole daily before breakfast
answerChoices.rationale: The clearance and mucosal findings support a reflux-injury target. Daily conventional delayed-release omeprazole has been taken away from a meal. Optimize its administration before judging that regimen insufficient or adding therapy.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole before breakfast and before dinner
answerChoices.rationale: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.

answerChoices.label: Use daily prebreakfast omeprazole with as-needed bedtime famotidine
answerChoices.rationale: Famotidine provides H2-receptor acid suppression, and selected patients have a role for as-needed bedtime H2 blockade for nocturnal symptoms during optimized PPI use. Adding it while first correcting PPI administration escalates treatment before the response to that correction is known.

decisionNodes.explanation: Prompt passage with distal mucosal injury shifts the present target toward reflux rather than another junction procedure. record.title: Foregut record review — salvage before resection
fairness: Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication is a defensible offered salvage referral. The combination of relatively favorable esophageal geometry, residual junction restriction and incomplete prior muscle division supports addressing a remaining outlet target before organ resection.

Esophagectomy is a credible near-miss after both dilation and POEM have failed. The resident must distinguish a correctable treatment deficit from irreversible reservoir failure; fitness for major surgery does not by itself select the most radical operation.

The description that division stopped short of the gastric extension is decisive clinical evidence rather than an unfair lexical match: none of the options simply repeats that phrase. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

Other salvage approaches may also warrant specialist consideration, but they are not offered; this does not invalidate the relative ranking here. The explanation properly frames Heller as a consideration rather than a universally mandatory rescue.

The historical referral is explicitly identified in both update and task, so it is not confused with the present post-aspiration visit. The node stands alone and sets up a distinct later reassessment. This is a high-yield salvage-versus-resection principle. PASS is editorial, not clinical approval.
suggestions: Optional presentation cleanup: replace the game-role phrase 'The founder reviews' with a direct description of reviewing the earlier and current records.
Keep the exact historical timepoint visible and preserve the explanation's conditional specialist framing. Do not generalize this answer to all patients with prior failed POEM.

reviewEntries.title: Investigation of recurrent symptoms after POEM
clarityIssues: The standalone Presentation and Current update never state the original diagnosis or indication for POEM. 'The later record documents POEM' and 'no residual premature contractions' do not establish that she had achalasia; POEM is also used for other motor disorders. A resident should not have to recover that prerequisite from the topic title or a removed companion.

'The later record' is a residual sequence reference. The treatment-response-recurrence chronology is otherwise understandable, and the task completely identifies the current investigation decision. Naming the postoperative reassessment directly would make the standalone frame cleaner.
fairness: The proposed reasoning is meaningful: interpret reassuring pressure findings without equating them with adequate bolus clearance, then choose an investigation for recurrent food hold-up while considering reflux and luminal disease. This supports a moderate two-step prediction, not a measured difficulty claim.

Timed barium assessment is a defensible intended answer for recurrent symptoms after achalasia treatment. However, the visible candidate does not establish that prerequisite. I cannot endorse the explanation's unqualified 'Recurrent food hold-up after POEM warrants timed barium assessment first' as a universal ordering rule for every POEM indication.

Endoscopy remains a credible competing investigation for recurrent dysphagia and possible post-treatment mucosal injury or narrowing. Maintained weight and hydration establish stability but do not exclude these mechanisms. This is a missing-context/ranking concern, not a claim that endoscopy is definitely superior or that the intended key is clinically wrong.

All three options are specific investigations at the same decision stage, with comparable specificity. No material wording-overlap, length-outlier, convergence, absolute, diagnosis-label or pre-answer teaching shortcut was identified. The pressure observations are relevant clinical data, not a nonmedical lexical match to the key.

This is now a single-node case: no earlier feedback supplies the answer and no later result is needed. Its main standalone deficit is the omitted treatment indication. Evaluating recurrent dysphagia after achalasia therapy is high-yield general-surgery learning content; that is an editorial scope judgment, not a verified exam-frequency claim.
Offline review of the supplied candidate only; no fresh guideline verification or clinical approval. The unique ranking should be confirmed by Melissa Rowland after the missing context is repaired.
suggestions: State the documented original indication for POEM in the Presentation or Current update. If the intended case is treated achalasia, name that established history; a known diagnosis is appropriate in this management task. Do not infer or invent the indication from the procedure alone.

Keep the normal pressure findings, recurrent food hold-up and stable intake. Recheck timed barium versus endoscopy under the explicitly stated diagnosis; do not remove endoscopy by inserting a teaching sentence or a gratuitous normal endoscopy result.

Scope the explanation's first-test recommendation to the established clinical condition and explain why endoscopy is complementary in this particular decision. If the original indication was a non-achalasia spastic disorder, obtain clinical review of the ordering rather than importing the achalasia pathway.
Replace the dangling 'later record' reference with a direct postoperative reassessment reference. Preserve the two-step pressure-versus-clearance distinction and parallel test labels.

reviewEntries.title: Organ-preserving salvage after an incomplete myotomy
fairness: The task and Current update explicitly anchor the decision to the earlier referral. Although the Presentation mentions a subsequent aspiration-related admission, the operative-fitness statement and all decision-critical studies are assigned to the earlier timepoint. No absent companion is needed to answer this retrospective question.

Two consequential steps remain: combine junction hold-up, reduced distensibility and the operative endpoint to identify residual junction resistance with an incomplete treatment target; then use the relatively straight esophagus and operative fitness to favor organ-preserving salvage over resection or temporary palliation.

Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication is the best offered referral. Esophagectomy represents prematurely equating failure of two interventions with exhausted organ function; botulinum injection underuses a definitive salvage opportunity in a patient fit for surgery. Neither distractor is equally supported by the supplied record. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The explanation appropriately says 'support considering Heller salvage' and retains specialized foregut assessment. It does not establish Heller as the only possible retreatment in every failed-POEM patient; alternative endoscopic salvage is outside this option set and should not be declared categorically inappropriate.

The phrases 'relatively straight esophagus', 'Distensibility remained reduced' and 'muscle division had stopped short of the gastric extension' are strong clinical discriminators, but none gives a nonmedical wording match to one option. The options share referral grammar and comparable length; there is no material convergence, absolute, uniquely cautious key or pre-answer treatment instruction.

This is moderate rather than hard: the technical shortfall and fitness substantially narrow the decision, but selecting organ preservation despite prior treatment failures still tests a consequential resident error. Salvage before esophagectomy is a high-yield foregut principle; no exact testing frequency is asserted.

The standalone case has one scored node, so there is no later-part coherence issue or preceding-feedback scaffold. This editorial PASS follows offline review of the supplied candidate and does not confer clinical approval; the draft remains needs_clinician_review.
suggestions: Optional presentation cleanup: replace 'The founder reviews' with a direct chart-review description, and streamline the earlier/current-record frame around the historical decision. These are not answer-blocking defects.

answerChoices.rationale: Normal measured relaxation and absence of residual spasm do not establish bolus emptying. Upright timed barium testing directly assesses clearance and is the ACG first-line objective investigation for recurrent symptoms after definitive achalasia treatment.

answerChoices.rationale: Nocturnal fluid return after POEM makes reflux a credible mechanism. Her recurrent food hold-up still requires objective clearance assessment first; reflux monitoring answers a different question once clearance and structural findings have been considered.

decisionNodes.stem: Which medication plan should next address {patientName}'s persistent symptoms after POEM?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The subsequent upright timed examination shows prompt liquid clearance and tablet passage into the stomach. Endoscopy shows distal mucosal breaks, without retained food or a fixed narrowing. She describes burning and sour fluid return, especially after lying down. Bottle review confirms conventional delayed-release omeprazole taken every day at bedtime, several hours after dinner.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole daily before breakfast
answerChoices.rationale: The clearance and mucosal findings support a reflux-injury target. Daily conventional delayed-release omeprazole has been taken away from a meal. Optimize its administration before judging that regimen insufficient or adding therapy.

answerChoices.label: Use omeprazole before breakfast and before dinner
answerChoices.rationale: Twice-daily PPI use can be appropriate after persistent disease despite an optimized daily regimen. The present record has not tested properly administered daily therapy, so increasing treatment now skips that correction.

answerChoices.label: Use daily prebreakfast omeprazole with as-needed bedtime famotidine
answerChoices.rationale: Famotidine provides H2-receptor acid suppression, and selected patients have a role for as-needed bedtime H2 blockade for nocturnal symptoms during optimized PPI use. Adding it while first correcting PPI administration escalates treatment before the response to that correction is known.

decisionNodes.explanation: Prompt passage with distal mucosal injury shifts the present target toward reflux rather than another junction procedure. decisionNodes.stem: Which plan best fits {patientName}'s earlier referral after dilation and POEM had failed?
decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At that earlier referral she was fit for major surgery but continued to retain food after graded dilation and POEM. The timed study showed a relatively straight esophagus with hold-up at the junction. Endoscopy showed no reflux stricture or malignancy. Distensibility remained reduced, and review of the POEM report documented that the muscle division had stopped short of the gastric extension.

answerChoices.rationale: The record identifies an incomplete prior myotomy and anatomy conducive to salvage. Guidance supports considering Heller before resection in this setting.

answerChoices.rationale: Temporary symptom relief is appropriate when definitive therapy is unsuitable. Her fitness and residual correctable target support considering definitive salvage here.

decisionNodes.stem: Which referral best fits {patientName}'s current outside-hospital findings?

record.title: Foregut record review — salvage before resection
fairness: Heller myotomy with partial fundoplication is a defensible offered salvage referral. The combination of relatively favorable esophageal geometry, residual junction restriction and incomplete prior muscle division supports addressing a remaining outlet target before organ resection.

Esophagectomy is a credible near-miss after both dilation and POEM have failed. The resident must distinguish a correctable treatment deficit from irreversible reservoir failure; fitness for major surgery does not by itself select the most radical operation.

The description that division stopped short of the gastric extension is decisive clinical evidence rather than an unfair lexical match: none of the options simply repeats that phrase. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

Other salvage approaches may also warrant specialist consideration, but they are not offered; this does not invalidate the relative ranking here. The explanation properly frames Heller as a consideration rather than a universally mandatory rescue.
